nodes.label: Card c001: MPS elevated 24-48h; 20-40g protein across 3-5 meals
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Aragon & Schoenfeld (2013) is misordered (Schoenfeld is second author); paper supports rejecting the anabolic-window myth and gives 0.4-0.5 g/kg LBM per meal, but contains no 24-48h MPS statement.
nodes.norm_label: card c001: mps elevated 24-48h; 20-40g protein across 3-5 meals

nodes.label: Card c002: stretch>contraction; slow eccentrics produce more hypertrophy per joule
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Maeo 2021 is Med Sci Sports Exerc, not Eur J Sport Sci. Long-length half supported; tempo half contradicted by Schoenfeld/Ogborn/Krieger 2015 (hypertrophy similar 0.5-8s). 'Per joule' is not a reported quantity.
nodes.norm_label: card c002: stretch>contraction; slow eccentrics produce more hypertrophy per joule

nodes.label: Card c003: Epley 1RM formula w*(1+reps/30); 100x5->116kg; ~5% accurate
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Epley 1985 is a self-published, non-peer-reviewed poundage chart. Arithmetic itself is off: 100*(1+5/30)=116.7, not 116. The '~5% accurate for trained lifters' claim is unsupported (Reynolds 2006 reports SEE 1.85-14.05 kg).
nodes.norm_label: card c003: epley 1rm formula w*(1+reps/30); 100x5->116kg; ~5% accurate

nodes.label: Card c004: 1996 caffeine/creatine paper used 5mg/kg co-ingested; modern reviews find no interaction
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Trexler & Smith-Ryan (2015) journal mis-cited. The card inverts its own source: the 2015 review states caffeine 'may blunt the ergogenic effect of creatine'. The 1996 paper (Vandenberghe) used 6-day dosing, not single-dose.
nodes.norm_label: card c004: 1996 caffeine/creatine paper used 5mg/kg co-ingested; modern reviews find no interaction

nodes.label: Card c005: 10-20 sets/wk optimal volume; curve flattens at 22-25 sets
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Schoenfeld 2017 (verified) supports the graded dose-response (+0.023 ES/set, P=0.002) but the '10-20' band and '22-25 plateau' are not in the paper; the model is linear and detects no plateau at all.
nodes.norm_label: card c005: 10-20 sets/wk optimal volume; curve flattens at 22-25 sets

nodes.label: Card c006: 8h sleep raises T 10-15% vs 5h; GH in 4-5 pulses; one bad night costs 4-6% strength
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Leproult & Van Cauter 2011: the 8h condition was an at-home run-in, not the comparator; direction is inverted (restriction decreased daytime T). GH and strength claims are absent from this citation.
nodes.norm_label: card c006: 8h sleep raises t 10-15% vs 5h; gh in 4-5 pulses; one bad night costs 4-6% strength

nodes.label: Card c007 'Vyvanse and the heart': LDX raises HR 5-15bpm, SBP 3-7mmHg — MUST BE DELETED (Section 7, medical content)
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Coghill 2014 Table 2 at 70mg reports +4.1-5.4bpm/+1.3-2.6mmHg; the card's ranges are ~3x and non-overlapping.
nodes.norm_label: card c007 'vyvanse and the heart': ldx raises hr 5-15bpm, sbp 3-7mmhg — must be deleted (section 7, medical content)

nodes.label: Card c008: DOMS is not a proxy for training quality
nodes.rationale: WRONG (journal only, science sound) — Nosaka/Newton/Sacco 2002 is Scand J Med Sci Sports, not MSSE. The underlying claim is well supported (higher damage doses did not increase soreness, r<0.32).
nodes.norm_label: card c008: doms is not a proxy for training quality

nodes.label: Card c009: protein TEF 25-30%; net 600 of 800 kcal
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Westerterp verbatim gives 20-30% for protein; card narrows without warrant, and the arithmetic double-counts TEF by subtracting it from intake while also using an activity-factor TDEE.
nodes.norm_label: card c009: protein tef 25-30%; net 600 of 800 kcal

nodes.label: Card c010: deep squats produce less knee shear than partial squats
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Hartmann 2013 headline supported but mechanism wrong: compressive stress (not shear) peaks near 90 degrees; posterior/PCL shear is actually higher at parallel depth than quarter depth.
nodes.norm_label: card c010: deep squats produce less knee shear than partial squats

nodes.label: Card c011: tonnage is a useful stimulus proxy; ~6 million kg cumulative
nodes.rationale: WRONG (twice) — Mangine 2015 cuts against the card (lower-tonnage group gained more lean mass and strength); the app's own computed cumulative tonnage is ~0.6-0.8 million kg, an order of magnitude below the claimed 6 million.
nodes.norm_label: card c011: tonnage is a useful stimulus proxy; ~6 million kg cumulative

nodes.label: Card c012: Robusta 2.2-2.7% vs arabica 1.2-1.5% caffeine; condensed milk macros; stick ~120mg
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Belay 2008 is an Ethiopian-arabica-only analytical paper containing none of the cited numbers and no robusta data.
nodes.norm_label: card c012: robusta 2.2-2.7% vs arabica 1.2-1.5% caffeine; condensed milk macros; stick ~120mg

nodes.label: Card c013 'Hydration and Vyvanse': amphetamines reduce thirst; 3-4 L/day; dehydration causes headaches — MUST BE DELETED (Section 7, medical content)
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Boellner 2010 is a pediatric (ages 6-12) single-dose PK study in Clinical Therapeutics, not Pediatrics, and says nothing about thirst, dehydration or headache.
nodes.norm_label: card c013 'hydration and vyvanse': amphetamines reduce thirst; 3-4 l/day; dehydration causes headaches — must be deleted (section 7, medical content)

nodes.label: Card c014: push-up loads 64% BW; 41% at 30deg elevation; 74% at 30deg decline
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Suprak 2011 studied only traditional/knees-down push-ups; the 64/41/74 triple belongs to Ebben 2011, which used box heights (61.0 cm), not angles.
nodes.norm_label: card c014: push-up loads 64% bw; 41% at 30deg elevation; 74% at 30deg decline

nodes.label: Card c015: whey peaks 60-90min, casein 3-4h; leucine +220-280% vs +90-120%
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Boirie 1997: casein peaked at the same ~80min as whey; its distinguishing feature is duration, not delayed peak. No numeric plasma leucine percentages are reported; real Ra-ratio values are ~283%/~132%.
nodes.norm_label: card c015: whey peaks 60-90min, casein 3-4h; leucine +220-280% vs +90-120%

nodes.label: Card u001: stapedius ~1mm, smallest skeletal muscle
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Gray's Anatomy 42nd ed supports 'smallest skeletal muscle' but pooled mean length is 3.77-4.91mm, roughly 4-5x the card's figure.
nodes.norm_label: card u001: stapedius ~1mm, smallest skeletal muscle

nodes.label: Card u002: soleus 80-90% slow-twitch; orbicularis oculi ~100% fast; rarely shifts past 70:30
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Johnson 1973 metadata correct; soleus 80-90% COULD NOT VERIFY (secondary sources split ~70-87%); orbicularis oculi likely not among the 36 studied muscles and measured values are ~82-92% type II; the 70:30 training claim has no source.
nodes.norm_label: card u002: soleus 80-90% slow-twitch; orbicularis oculi ~100% fast; rarely shifts past 70:30

nodes.label: Card u003: Milo of Croton as the earliest reference to progressive overload
nodes.rationale: SUPPORTED — Quintilian's Institutio Oratoria I.9.5 verified; noted as a rhetorical chria (teaching example), not a training account.
nodes.norm_label: card u003: milo of croton as the earliest reference to progressive overload

nodes.label: Card u004: creatine isolated 1832 by Chevreul from meat broth; Harris 1992 showed oral loading works
nodes.rationale: SUPPORTED — Harris 1992 loading data verified; minor imprecision, Chevreul used an alkaline water extract of skeletal muscle, not 'meat broth'.
nodes.norm_label: card u004: creatine isolated 1832 by chevreul from meat broth; harris 1992 showed oral loading works

nodes.label: Card u005: 2x/wk gives ~3.1% more growth than 1x in trained lifters; 3x adds nothing
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Schoenfeld/Ogborn/Krieger 2016: the 3.1% figure (95% CI 1.6-4.6, P=0.003) is correctly transcribed, but the pooled cohorts were dominated by untrained subjects, not 'trained lifters', and the paper explicitly could not resolve 3x/week. See Section 2: Schoenfeld 2019 later showed this frequency effect is a volume artifact.
nodes.norm_label: card u005: 2x/wk gives ~3.1% more growth than 1x in trained lifters; 3x adds nothing

nodes.label: Card u006: trap bar gives 20-30% lower lumbar shear; 5-8% slower bar speed
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Camara 2016 measured EMG and force/power/velocity, not lumbar shear; the velocity claim is backwards (trap bar ~11% faster). The lumbar claim traces to Swinton 2011, which reported lower peak moments, not shear.
nodes.norm_label: card u006: trap bar gives 20-30% lower lumbar shear; 5-8% slower bar speed

nodes.label: Card u007: lifters are 5-10x stronger in horizontal push than pull
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Cools 2007 is an EMG scapular-activation study in Am J Sports Med (mis-cited journal), containing no push-vs-pull strength comparison; measured push:pull 1RM ratios cluster near 1:1.
nodes.norm_label: card u007: lifters are 5-10x stronger in horizontal push than pull

nodes.label: Card u008: untrained men gain 4-6kg lean yr1, 2-3 yr2, ~1 yr3
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Lambert & Flynn 2002 is a review of fatigue mechanisms in bodybuilding, containing no year-by-year gain figures; no peer-reviewed primary source was found for the table.
nodes.norm_label: card u008: untrained men gain 4-6kg lean yr1, 2-3 yr2, ~1 yr3

nodes.label: Card u009: 3mg/kg caffeine cuts RPE 5-7%, improves time-to-exhaustion 3-5%
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Grgic 2020 (card cites the DOI-suffix year 2019 in error) umbrella review reports no 3mg/kg dose-specific effect; RPE -5.6% is consistent but the endurance improvement was actually 12.3% (95% CI 9.1-15.4), not 3-5%.
nodes.norm_label: card u009: 3mg/kg caffeine cuts rpe 5-7%, improves time-to-exhaustion 3-5%

nodes.label: Card u010: heavy lifting >80% 1RM is one of only three things that raise adult bone density
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Watson 2018 (LIFTMOR) threshold was >85% 1RM, not >80%; population was postmenopausal women only (T-score<-1.0); the paper makes no 'only three things' claim.
nodes.norm_label: card u010: heavy lifting >80% 1rm is one of only three things that raise adult bone density

nodes.label: Card u011: by 80, ~40% of fast-twitch fibres lost vs ~10-15% slow-twitch; heavy training the most important anti-ageing modality
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Faulkner 2007 reports ~50% TOTAL fibre loss by 80 with no fibre-type split in the abstract; the 40/10-15 split is COULD NOT VERIFY; the superlative is not the paper's, whose conclusion is that atrophy 'can be slowed, but not halted'.
nodes.norm_label: card u011: by 80, ~40% of fast-twitch fibres lost vs ~10-15% slow-twitch; heavy training the most important anti-ageing modality

nodes.label: Card u012: Galen recorded Theagenes eating an entire ox
nodes.rationale: WRONG — the anecdote is Athenaeus's (Deipnosophists 10.412-413, citing Poseidippus), not Galen's; Athenaeus separately attributes an ox-eating feat to Milo, not Theagenes.
nodes.norm_label: card u012: galen recorded theagenes eating an entire ox

nodes.label: Card u013: discs lose ~20% water 30->60; heavy spinal loading is protective
nodes.rationale: WRONG (reverses its source) — Adams & Roughley 2006 states 'excessive mechanical loading disrupts a disc's structure' and lists loading history among the CAUSES of degeneration, not a protective factor.
nodes.norm_label: card u013: discs lose ~20% water 30->60; heavy spinal loading is protective

nodes.label: Card u014: ONE hard set/muscle/week within 2 reps of failure maintains ~95% strength for 8-12 weeks
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Bickel/Cross/Bamman 2011: maintenance phase was 32 weeks, not 8-12; the leanest dose was 3 sets/wk, not one; effort was volitional fatigue, not 2 RIR; after 32 weeks of complete detraining strength fell only 7%.
nodes.norm_label: card u014: one hard set/muscle/week within 2 reps of failure maintains ~95% strength for 8-12 weeks

nodes.label: Card u015: 10wk heavy squats improve 5km running economy 5% via stiffer Achilles and faster ground contact
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Storen 2008 duration was 8 weeks, not 10; the 5% economy figure is right but measured at 70% VO2max, not '5km economy'; the paper measured neither tendon stiffness nor ground contact time.
nodes.norm_label: card u015: 10wk heavy squats improve 5km running economy 5% via stiffer achilles and faster ground contact

nodes.label: Card r001: soleus has the highest mitochondrial density of any human muscle; >25% MVC for hours; stand every 30min
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Hamilton 2022 contains zero occurrences of 'mitochondrial density' and characterises the soleus at ~88% type I with no %MVC reported; the standing-break claim is contradicted by the paper's own cited source (standing did not reduce glucose vs sitting).
nodes.norm_label: card r001: soleus has the highest mitochondrial density of any human muscle; >25% mvc for hours; stand every 30min

nodes.label: Card r002: Galen linked diet/training/recovery first; prescribed pork and beans; banned from Rome for ridiculing Hippocrates
nodes.rationale: WRONG — wrong Galen title cited; the 'banned from Rome' claim is backwards (Galen venerated Hippocrates); 'pork and beans' is contradicted by Losch 2014's gladiator-diet study (wheat, barley, legumes).
nodes.norm_label: card r002: galen linked diet/training/recovery first; prescribed pork and beans; banned from rome for ridiculing hippocrates

nodes.label: Card r003: MSTN knockout child lifted 3kg dumbbells at age 4
nodes.rationale: SUPPORTED — Schuelke 2004 verified; correction: the child was 4.5 years old, not 4.
nodes.norm_label: card r003: mstn knockout child lifted 3kg dumbbells at age 4

nodes.label: Card r004: women's pull-up capacity equals men's once strength-to-mass is controlled
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Vanderburgh & Flanagan 2000 is an unrelated male-only backpack-run study with no pull-ups or women; Miller 1993 shows women only ~52% as strong as men in the upper body, with equality only in force per unit muscle cross-sectional area.
nodes.norm_label: card r004: women's pull-up capacity equals men's once strength-to-mass is controlled

nodes.label: Card r005: resistance training depresses immunity 2-24h; gym-goers get ~40% fewer URTIs
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Walsh 2011 makes no resistance-training immunosuppression claim and questions the 'open window' itself; the 40% figure actually traces to Nieman 2011 (43% fewer URTI days, for AEROBIC exercise, self-reported).
nodes.norm_label: card r005: resistance training depresses immunity 2-24h; gym-goers get ~40% fewer urtis

nodes.label: Card r006: Topham lifted ~800kg; mid-thigh pull 270kg
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — the ~800kg (1,836 lb / 833 kg) hogshead feat is independently documented via a contemporary etching; the 270kg mid-thigh-pull figure is COULD NOT VERIFY.
nodes.norm_label: card r006: topham lifted ~800kg; mid-thigh pull 270kg

nodes.label: Card r007: exercise rhinitis from parasympathetic rebound after sympathetic arousal
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Silvers 1991 is in Annals of Allergy, not J Allergy Clin Immunol, and shows cold-induced rhinorrhoea is cholinergic, not parasympathetic rebound; exercise itself normally produces sympathetic nasal decongestion.
nodes.norm_label: card r007: exercise rhinitis from parasympathetic rebound after sympathetic arousal

nodes.label: Card r008: one night total sleep deprivation cuts 1RM bench 8-12%; 4h x3 nights cuts 5-8%
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Reilly & Piercy 1994 used 3-hour sleep for 3 nights with no total-deprivation arm, so the card's headline has no basis in the cited paper; the specific percentages are COULD NOT VERIFY.
nodes.norm_label: card r008: one night total sleep deprivation cuts 1rm bench 8-12%; 4h x3 nights cuts 5-8%

nodes.label: Card r009: 85-90% of early strength gain is neural; visible growth starts weeks 6-10
nodes.rationale: UNSUPPORTED — Sale 1988's treatment is qualitative with no locatable 85-90% figure; Bontemps 2022 measured vastus lateralis ACSA growth of +2.9% at 2 weeks, contradicting the 'weeks 6-10' onset claim.
nodes.norm_label: card r009: 85-90% of early strength gain is neural; visible growth starts weeks 6-10

nodes.label: Card r010: blinded milk-vs-soy trials found identical 'mucus feeling'
nodes.rationale: WRONG (cites one paper, describes another) — the card cites Pinnock 1990 (no soy arm, no blinding); the design it actually describes is Pinnock & Arney 1993, where 3 of 14 indicators rose equally in both arms.
nodes.norm_label: card r010: blinded milk-vs-soy trials found identical 'mucus feeling'

nodes.label: Card r011: ice baths within 24h cut hypertrophy 25-30%
nodes.rationale: WRONG — Roberts 2015: cold-water immersion was applied within 5 minutes, not 24 hours; the real effect was ~67% less lean-mass gain than active recovery, and type II fibre CSA did not grow at all with CWI.
nodes.norm_label: card r011: ice baths within 24h cut hypertrophy 25-30%

nodes.label: Card r012: grip strength at 40 predicts mortality better than SBP or BMI; -5kg -> +16% risk over the following decade
nodes.rationale: PARTIALLY — Leong 2015 (PURE study): HR 1.16 per 5kg and the SBP comparison are verbatim supported, but median follow-up was 4.0 years, not a decade; the cohort was aged 35-70 at enrolment, so 'at age 40' misdescribes it; BMI was an adjustment covariate, not a comparator.
nodes.norm_label: card r012: grip strength at 40 predicts mortality better than sbp or bmi; -5kg -> +16% risk over the following decade

nodes.label: P2 Profile, Nutrition, Plan Generator Implementation Plan
nodes.norm_label: p2 profile, nutrition, plan generator implementation plan

nodes.label: Mifflin-St Jeor RMR equation
nodes.rationale: Used when body fat is unknown. Chosen over Harris-Benedict/Roza-Shizgal because Frankenfield 2013 found it accurate in 82% of n=337 and unbiased (95% CI -26 to +8 kcal/d) where the others overestimated.

nodes.label: Cunningham RMR equation (FFM-based)
nodes.rationale: RMR = 370 + 21.6 x FFM(kg), used when body fat is known. Widely mislabelled 'Katch-McArdle' but published by Cunningham (1991); must not be confused with Cunningham's own 1980 equation 500 + 22*LBM.

nodes.label: FAO/WHO/UNU PAL activity-factor bands
nodes.rationale: Three verified PAL bands (1.40-1.69 / 1.70-1.99 / 2.00-2.40) mapped onto five ActivityLevel categories; the two interior points (light 1.55, active 1.85) are within-band midpoints, labelled HEURISTIC and surfaced in basis.activityFactor.

nodes.label: Fat-loss rate prescription (0.7% BW/week)
nodes.rationale: Target rate 0.7 %BW/week, bounded 0.5-1.0 %BW/week. This is a prescribed target the plan is evaluated against, not a value derived from the kcal deficit, because no verified kcal-to-mass-change coefficient exists.

nodes.label: Muscle-gain energy surplus (500 kcal/day)
nodes.rationale: 500 kcal/day sits inside the measured 506+/-84 kcal/day. expectedRateKgPerWeek is null for this goal: the source study reports total gain but not study duration, so no weekly rate can be derived, and a separate paper states the required surplus is unknown.

nodes.label: Protein target rules (body-mass vs FFM denominators)
nodes.rationale: Maintenance and muscle gain use g/kg body mass; a fat-loss deficit uses g/kg fat-free mass. The denominators are kept strictly separate because applying the FFM range to body mass is a roughly 33% overfeed at 25% body fat. Falls back to the body-mass row when no body-fat estimate exists.
nodes.norm_label: protein target rules (body-mass vs ffm denominators)

nodes.label: IOM beverage fluid target (3000/2200 mL)
nodes.rationale: The IOM total-water AI is 3.7 L men / 2.7 L women; beverages supply the 3.0 L / 2.2 L figures used here because an app cannot measure water from food. Replaces the legacy flat 3.5 L target, which is sex-invariant and mis-sized for both sexes.

nodes.label: Creatine dosing rule
nodes.rationale: max(3 g, 0.1 g/kg body mass), capped at 10 g/day. Dosed by body mass, not sex, because neither source paper gives a sex-specific dose.

nodes.label: Independent computation of intake target and expected rate
nodes.decision: compute targetKcal and expectedRateKgPerWeek independently rather than deriving one from the other
nodes.rationale: No verified coefficient converts a kcal deficit into a weekly mass change: the 3500 kcal/lb rule is rejected outright, and the literature's replacement ('10 kcal/day per pound of weight change') is a steady-state relation taking about a year to reach half its effect, not a weekly rate. targetKcal is therefore an intake prescription and expectedRateKgPerWeek a separately prescribed target rate; basis.rateRule states this.
nodes.norm_label: independent computation of intake target and expected rate

nodes.label: 3500 kcal/lb conversion rule (rejected)
nodes.decision: reject the 3500 kcal/lb rule as a kcal-to-mass-change conversion
nodes.rationale: Rejected outright by Hall 2011 as a discredited energy-balance heuristic; no verified replacement coefficient exists in the evidence base, so the engine computes intake and expected rate independently instead.

nodes.label: Gym PAL ladder 1.2/1.375/1.55/1.725/1.9 (rejected)
nodes.decision: reject the ubiquitous gym PAL ladder as the activity-factor source
nodes.rationale: No primary source exists for this ladder; its interior points are arithmetic interpolations and its 1.2 anchor is a non-ambulant limit, whereas FAO/WHO/UNU 2004 puts the free-living floor at 1.40.

nodes.label: src/domain/bodyfat.ts US Navy tape method (metric)
nodes.rationale: Implements only the metric density form, not the DoD imperial linearisation, because the two are not algebraically equivalent and mixing them introduces a silent 0.3-0.7 %BF disagreement. The female equation's hip term is explicitly guarded against a known published typo (Potter 2022) that omits it.

nodes.label: secondaryMuscles field and direct/indirect set counting
nodes.decision: add Exercise.secondaryMuscles: string[] to the master plan section 5 type
nodes.rationale: The cited counting rule (a direct set counts 1.0, an indirect set 0.5) cannot be implemented against a single undifferentiated muscleGroups array. Which muscles are secondary for a given lift is an engineering judgement inside the cited rule: a muscle is secondary only when it is a dynamic assisting mover, never an isometric stabiliser.
nodes.norm_label: secondarymuscles field and direct/indirect set counting

nodes.label: Barbell row (heavier) exercise (excluded, unsafe cue)
nodes.decision: exclude the heavy barbell row from the exercise library
nodes.rationale: Content peer review section 6 marks its cue WRONG (unsafe): it permits a slight cheat / TnT on a loaded hip-hinge, contradicting the same file's own rounding-lower-back injury warning. May return only if the cue is rewritten to the strict standard.

nodes.label: Weekly set band by day count
nodes.rationale: Bands of 6-10 / 9-15 / 12-16 / 14-18 / 16-20 fractional sets per muscle per week by day count. With 13 muscle groups no achievable session length puts every muscle in band (~180 sets/week), so each template declares bandMuscles and reports the rest as maintenance-only, per the content review's own sanctioned alternative.

nodes.label: Rest interval rule by load class (180/120/90s)

nodes.label: Deload volume-cut rule (41-60%, load unchanged)
nodes.rationale: setModifier = 0.5 sits inside the measured 41-60% optimal-taper volume reduction 'without any modification of either training intensity or frequency'; loadModifier = 1 is the verbatim finding. The legacy 'reduce weight by 40%' approach is the reverse of this finding and is not implemented.

nodes.label: Four-week deload cadence (calendar backstop)
nodes.rationale: Three training weeks then one deload week, repeated. Explicitly labelled a calendar backstop, not an evidence-based interval: cited panels report 100% agreement that deload frequency depends on individual response and that pre-planned deloads might not be necessary; another study found a mid-programme deload gave no hypertrophy benefit. Autoregulation is deferred to a later plan.

nodes.label: Attendance-Driven Plan Cursor
nodes.rationale: PlanCursor.nextSessionIndex plus one status field per day (SessionAssignment.status) is the single authority on programme position, advancing only on complete or skip. Replaces the legacy programPosition(startDate, today) (console-store.jsx:68-77), a pure function of calendar dates with no attendance input: code review A11 shows a user training days 1-3 then travelling 10 days returns to 'day 14, Full Rest', leaving days 4-13 unreachable. A8 (todayISO() reads the UTC date) and A9 (isoDaysBetween loses a day across spring-forward) made the derived position wrong by a day for months. A12: before/after-programme branches produced plausible-looking wrong states nothing read. A13: nothing recomputed position at midnight. A62: the legacy SkipSession wrote s.skipped[week-day], a key with no reader. A63: 'done' had three incompatible definitions across three views. Contract pins: completeSession/skipSession are no-ops on an already-terminal assignment (so the cursor can never advance twice for one day); completedOn is stamped by whichever transition passes the last session, using the LocalDate argument, never a clock.

nodes.label: Half-Open Pause Interval [from, to)
nodes.rationale: A PlanPause covers the half-open local-date interval [from, to): from is the first paused day, to is the first day the plan is active again, and to === null means the pause is open. Chosen because the Today view's Resume control passes to = todayLocal(...); an inclusive end would make Resume a no-op for the day it was pressed, so the user pressing Resume this morning must get this morning's session. A resume date earlier than the pause start is clamped to a zero-length pause rather than treated as an error.

nodes.label: Pick-Today Swap Reshuffle
nodes.rationale: assignToday swaps sessions[target] and sessions[pick] inside the contiguous window [target, target+span-1] reachable within the current ISO week, rather than rotating the intervening sessions. A swap is not a rotation: the displaced session lands exactly where the picked one was, so the multiset of labels in the window (and the whole plan) is unchanged. Master plan §4 named this function reorderForToday, which appears nowhere else in the document; §6.4 and §6.7 both call it assignToday, so the plan amendment corrects the master plan's naming rather than the implementation.

nodes.label: PlannedSession Positional Ordinal Invariant
nodes.rationale: plan.sessions[i].ordinal === i + 1 for every i. assignToday's swap updates both swapped sessions' ordinal fields so the invariant survives a reshuffle; without it the displayed session numbers go out of order after a reorder. Requested as a master plan §5 amendment because the master plan stated no such invariant.

nodes.label: ISO Weekly Review Closure
nodes.rationale: An ISO week (Monday-Sunday, evaluated in the profile's own IANA timezone) is closed exactly once, only after it has fully ended, never while still running. delta = completed - target (negative = sessions missed). A week overlapped by any pause is paused=true and delta=0 so a deliberate pause never registers as a miss. Limitation recorded as a master-plan amendment: target is read from the profile's *current* Availability.weeklySessionTarget, so changing the weekly target retroactively changes the delta of every week not yet evaluated; no history of the target is stored.

nodes.label: PlanView.tsx
nodes.rationale: Code review A14: scrubbing the legacy week view silently changed the session shown under 'today is ...'. PlanView's week scrubber is deliberately a view of the session list, not a position, so moving it cannot desynchronise the programme.

nodes.label: Double Progression Engine
nodes.rationale: Percentage load increment gated by an equipment-step guard: when the top of the prescribed rep range is met on every prescribed set, add INCREMENT_FRACTION x working load (5% lower-compound, 2.5% upper-compound/isolation, ACSM 2009's cited 2-10% band), floored at one equipment step; when the smallest achievable step exceeds 10% of the working load (STEP_GUARD_FRACTION), extend the rep range instead of jumping load. A deload block is checked before the bodyweight rule (deload cuts volume and holds load; extending reps there would invert the block's purpose) — both branches tested. Code review A22: the legacy bumped the load mid-session after two sets; today's own logged sets never feed the suggestion. Code review A23: history is ordered by (assignmentDate, setNumber), never by loggedAt, because the legacy sorted by wall-clock timestamp so a retrospectively logged set could outrank real programme order.

nodes.label: No Fixed Hydration Volume / Drink-to-Thirst Cue
nodes.rationale: hydrationCue never prescribes a between-set volume: session-check says only 'Drink to thirst' every 20 minutes of an active session; daily-shortfall reports the beverage-target gap after 18:00 local; post-session-weigh asks for a body-mass check only if the profile opted in. The commonly cited '~1.5 L per kg lost' replacement figure is marked PARAPHRASE in the content review (publisher returned HTTP 402) and must not ship as a number.
nodes.norm_label: no fixed hydration volume / drink-to-thirst cue

nodes.label: Absolute-Instant Rest Timer
nodes.rationale: RestTimer is a pair of absolute instants {startedAt, endsAt}, never a decremented counter; remainingS is computed from endsAt and Date.now() and clamped at 0. Code review A31: the legacy chime lived inside a setInterval callback, and background tabs are throttled or (iOS) suspended, so a 90 s rest that ran while the phone was locked chimed 60 s late. extend() moves endsAt only, so totalS() (added as a master-plan amendment) is needed to know the timer's true span for the progress ring.

nodes.label: Legacy Flat 3.5 L Daily Fluid Rule
nodes.rationale: Rejected because a flat 3.5 L for everyone overshoots the female IOM 2005 beverage AI (2.2 L) by roughly 30% and undershoots the male AI (3.0 L), and is sex-invariant where the DRI is not.

nodes.rationale: Rejected as a hydration-target basis: Valtin H (2002) reports 'No scientific studies were found in support of 8 x 8.'

nodes.label: e1RM()
nodes.rationale: Epley estimate of a 1RM, validity domain reps<=10. Content peer review §5 (card c003) records Epley (1985) is self-published, not peer reviewed, N unknown; treat the output as an index for comparing sets, not a measured 1RM.

nodes.label: coachLine()
nodes.rationale: Ranked ladder (load PR > rep PR at same load > vs suggested load > vs prescribed range > top of range > inside range). Code review A5: legacy +-0.5/+-2.5 deadbands were unlabelled and compared against possibly-lb input, so on lb entry the 'over suggested' band collapsed to 0.5 lb and fired on nearly every set; bands are now declared in the display unit (OVER_BAND/UNDER_BAND) and converted exactly. Code review A25: 'weight PR' and 'overall record' shared one object/label; rung 1 is now explicitly a heaviest-load PR, rung 2 a rep PR at that load, neither claiming an e1RM record. Motivational filler ('pushing hard', 'save it for next set') is deleted per the global clinical-tone constraint.

nodes.label: defaultRestS()
nodes.rationale: Keys on Exercise.loadClass plus a rep ceiling (<=6 reps => heavy compound) because the literature stratifies rest by load and goal, not by exercise type; content review §9 states exercise-type stratification per se is INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE and this mapping is the closest faithful proxy onto the load ranges actually tested.

nodes.label: dailyBeverageTargetML()
nodes.rationale: Returns the sex-specific BEVERAGE share of the IOM 2005 total-water AI (male 3000 mL, female 2200 mL), not the total water intake figure (3.7 L / 2.7 L) which includes ~19% from food; the app can only observe beverages so it must never display the total-water number as a drink target.

nodes.label: store/training.ts
nodes.rationale: Pure AppState transformers only, no React, no I/O, no localStorage (code review A41: the store is the only writer). applyLogSet stores only the §5 fields (code review A28: the legacy froze the exercise name, both rep-range bounds, the suggestion and the lifetime-best object into every logged set). Bodyweight sets store loadKg 0 explicitly, never dropped as falsy (code review A60). applyAddCustomExercise assigns a stable generated id via newId(), never a positional index (code review A26: the legacy used 1000+i, so deleting one custom exercise re-attributed another's logged sets).

nodes.label: store/sessionMirror.ts
nodes.rationale: Mirrors only restTimer, activeAssignmentDate and bonusExerciseIds to sessionStorage; the six-second undo buffer is deliberately never mirrored, because a buffer that survived a reload would let a set be restored minutes later from a stale state.

Corrections applied per content review §6: strict-form 'cheat rep' language deleted from the barbell row; a Valsalva caution added to the back squat; the leg-press depth cap changed from a fixed knee angle to the lumbar-position limit; several unverifiable percentages (push-press +20%, stair-climber rail -30%, rower 'legs do 60%') deleted while keeping the directional statement; the weighted-pull-up-to-bodyweight-pull-up equivalence and the 'knee push-ups don't transfer' claim deleted outright; WARMUP_NOTICE added with no numeric prescription since no sourced protocol exists.

nodes.rationale: Reached through React context (VideoModalProvider/useVideoModal); window.__videoModal is gone. Iframe carries sandbox='allow-scripts allow-same-origin' and referrerPolicy='no-referrer' per master plan §8. The working Invidious host is persisted via setUi({videoInstanceHost}) rather than a direct localStorage write, honouring the lint gate that forbids localStorage outside persistence.ts.

nodes.rationale: Free-plan subrequest ceiling (50/invocation: 1+N KV reads, up to N writes, one fetch per due push) binds around N<=20 devices per cron tick before the daily KV read/write quotas would; stated as the number to watch, computed before Task 4 was implemented.

nodes.label: Single-send invariant
nodes.rationale: A reminder must be sent exactly once across repeated one-minute cron ticks, including after a client re-uploads an unchanged schedule; guaranteed by carrying the pruned 'sent' dedupe map forward through validatePut, selectDue's 15-minute window check, and markSent.

nodes.label: DST-aware reminder instant computation
nodes.rationale: computeReminderInstants converts wall-clock times through dates.ts so a DST transition inside the scheduling window shifts the epoch value while preserving local wall-clock time; the forward horizon is clamped in elapsed milliseconds (not calendar days) because 21 calendar days spanning a fall-back is 21d+1h, which the Worker would otherwise reject with 400.

nodes.label: CSP connect-src tightened to Worker origin
nodes.rationale: The baseline CSP's connect-src 'self' https://*.workers.dev is narrowed at build time to the exact deployed Worker origin, derived from VITE_REMINDER_API; a build with the variable unset fails closed to connect-src 'self' alone rather than shipping the wildcard.
nodes.norm_label: csp connect-src tightened to worker origin

nodes.label: Motivation Asset ArrayBuffer
nodes.rationale: The videos object store holds {id,name,type,size,data:ArrayBuffer,createdAt}; the Blob is rebuilt at read time with new Blob([data],{type}). ArrayBuffer is a core structured-clone type so it survives every IndexedDB implementation including fake-indexeddb+jsdom. Cost: file.arrayBuffer() materializes the whole clip in JS heap while saving (~150 MiB spike for a 150 MiB clip), so Settings copy steers users toward a clip of a few tens of MiB.

nodes.label: Motivation Asset Blob Direct Storage
nodes.rationale: Storing the File/Blob directly would let browsers store IndexedDB Blobs by reference, avoiding the heap spike, but cannot be tested: fake-indexeddb v5+ dropped its structuredClone polyfill and defers to Node's serializer, which does not recognize a jsdom Blob. Measured 2026-09-01 (vitest 4.1.11 / jsdom 30 / fake-indexeddb 6.2.5): db.put(store, jsdomBlob) then db.get returns {} silently — total data loss with no test coverage possible.

nodes.label: iOS video policy (no autoplay, gesture-required playback)
nodes.rationale: WebKit's iOS video policy requires playsinline (or Safari takes the video fullscreen), permits autoplay only when muted, and requires a user gesture to start playback with sound. The modal therefore carries playsinline, carries neither autoplay nor muted, and calls play() only inside the Play button's click handler; a muted autoplay was rejected because a silent confrontation clip defeats the feature's purpose.

nodes.label: Copy contract (default skin)
nodes.rationale: Binding on every UI task in P1 to P9. Rewritten 2026-09-02 against the three shipped copy tables so the document stops restating key lists that rot; what binds is R1 to R13 plus the suite in src/content/copy.test.ts.

nodes.label: Clinical default register
nodes.rationale: The default skin states what happened and what to do and nothing else. A skin may change register but may not change a number, a unit, or the meaning of a plan-altering control.

nodes.label: How a word is counted
nodes.rationale: Slots are removed first, punctuation stripped, and a token counts only if it contains a letter and is not a unit token, so 60 kg x 8 counts as zero words. A table that shouts a unit symbol is charged for the word.

nodes.label: Unit token list
nodes.rationale: s, kg, lb, mL, g, kcal, MiB, cm, mm, ms, the per cent sign and the multiplication sign are excluded from the word count. Capital S is deliberately absent because S is the siemens and the app measures no conductance.

nodes.label: R1. A button is at most three words
nodes.rationale: Applies to keys under button. in all three tables; decided mechanically by word count less the LENGTH_EXEMPT key.
nodes.norm_label: r1. a button is at most three words

nodes.label: R2. A hero is at most eight words
nodes.rationale: Keys under hero. carry the one line a screen is about, so the bound is tighter than an advice line.
nodes.norm_label: r2. a hero is at most eight words

nodes.label: R3. An advice line is at most twelve words
nodes.rationale: Keys under advice. The domain holds the same bound so a minted reason line cannot outrun the rule it is written under; surplus justification moves behind the R9 disclosure.
nodes.norm_label: r3. an advice line is at most twelve words

nodes.label: R4. A banner is at most two sentences
nodes.rationale: Sentence count splits after a full stop or question mark followed by a space, across all three tables, with no key exempt.
nodes.norm_label: r4. a banner is at most two sentences

nodes.label: R5. No em dash, and no en dash as a connector
nodes.rationale: U+2014 fails outright; U+2013 passes only between two digits, and a slot counts as a digit because the domain fills it with a number. The bare em dash placeholder for an absent value was withdrawn because the suite admits no exception, though a component may still draw one since a component is not a table.
nodes.norm_label: r5. no em dash, and no en dash as a connector

nodes.label: R6. No emoji
nodes.rationale: Four code point ranges are scanned (U+1F300-U+1FAFF, U+2600-U+27BF, U+FE0F, U+2B00-U+2BFF); the dingbat check and cross fall inside the second. Component chrome outside the tables may still draw a close cross or warning sign.

nodes.label: R7. No hedging and no filler
nodes.rationale: Left to review rather than the suite: a regular expression that pretended to decide it would pass bad copy and fail good copy.
nodes.norm_label: r7. no hedging and no filler

nodes.label: R8. No exclamation mark
nodes.rationale: Checked on the default table alone, because the clinical register states the count without motivational filler; an override may shout for its own reasons.

nodes.label: R9. Arithmetic goes behind a why? disclosure
nodes.rationale: A number is inlined only if the user must act differently because of it: a suggested load must be inline, how it was rounded must not. The disclosure is a details element whose summary is the literal why? for a derivation, and a domain function returns a separate why string rather than concatenating it.
nodes.norm_label: r9. arithmetic goes behind a why? disclosure

nodes.label: R10. Exempt content
nodes.rationale: Reference text a user chooses to open (form cues, exercise notes, Atlas card bodies and citations, the reminders runbook) is exempt from R1-R4 and R9 but never from R5, R6 or R11. Inside the tables the exemption is one key long and each entry names its call site so it can be revoked the day the call site changes.

nodes.label: R11. Name the defined quantity
nodes.rationale: Never a colloquial stand-in, in copy or identifiers: load or body mass rather than weight, kcal rather than calories, beverage intake (mL) rather than water. Left to review because nothing in a string says which quantity a word was meant to name. It also decides which words are keys: unit.characters is a key while cm, % and s are symbols.

nodes.label: R12. An override carries the unit symbol the default carries, verbatim
nodes.rationale: The case and the space are the symbol: +30 S DELAY states thirty siemens, not thirty seconds, and +30s states no SI quantity at all. Letting a register re-case the symbol with the sentence was rejected because it would let taste decide a quantity; the word count cannot catch the mistake since unit tokens are excluded from it, so the gate reads the default rather than the override.
nodes.norm_label: r12. an override carries the unit symbol the default carries, verbatim

nodes.label: R13. A control that closes for good never promises a return
nodes.rationale: Dismiss writes missHandled for the week and the screen does not come back, so now, later, soon or next in button.dismiss, button.cancel or button.close would state a postponement that never happens. Leaving it to review was rejected because the missed-week screen is where a skin is most tempted to be kind; the guarded keys are looked up by string so the rule stands before button.close has a CopyKey.
nodes.norm_label: r13. a control that closes for good never promises a return

nodes.label: LENGTH_EXEMPT map
nodes.rationale: One key long: advice.motivationClipLimit, which earns its place only by being rendered inside a details/summary why? block in src/ui/motivation/MotivationSettings.tsx. The call site is named so the exemption can be revoked when it changes.

nodes.label: DEFAULT_COPY (clinical table)
nodes.rationale: src/content/copy.ts is the union of record: 493 keys, 1888 words on 2026-09-02. The contract deliberately does not restate it, because a key list copied into prose rots the moment a task appends a key.

nodes.label: SKIN_COPY override map
nodes.rationale: Maps a skin id to a table; clinical maps to an empty object so the default stands unchanged. limelight and board are Partial<Record<CopyKey,string>> merged one key at a time, so an unlisted key falls through to the clinical string by design.

nodes.label: limelight override table
nodes.rationale: 120 rows, 379 words, 24.3 % coverage. Register is camp and lower case, aimed at the week or the app and never at the person reading. It records one verdict per fall-through group rather than one per key, so the 110 clinical keys carry a stated reason.

nodes.label: board override table
nodes.rationale: 37 rows, 68 words, 7.5 % coverage. Upper case throughout because a split-flap board has no lower case, with the upper case stopping at the one token that has no case to give (+30 s DELAY).

nodes.label: A board row exists only where a real airport term already names the thing
nodes.rationale: Every term must be a real airport term used in its real sense, so the humour comes from the discipline rather than from a joke. The moment the table invents a term it stops being a board.
nodes.norm_label: a board row exists only where a real airport term already names the thing

nodes.label: Mirror limelight's 120 rows on the board (rejected)
nodes.rationale: Rejected because matching limelight's coverage would mean minting airport words for a hydration shortfall, a body-mass check-in and a creatine dose. A board that announces irregular refreshment service about a glass of water is a joke in uniform.
nodes.norm_label: mirror limelight's 120 rows on the board (rejected)

nodes.label: The four rules binding both override tables
nodes.rationale: A skin changes words never facts; lower case everywhere in limelight except the shouted rows; no emoji in strings or comments (a pixel icon takes the position); and the joke never sits on a control whose misreading costs data.
nodes.norm_label: the four rules binding both override tables

nodes.label: The shouted rows (three keys, two strings)
nodes.rationale: button.startSession is LET'S GO BABES; status.prStamp and status.weekMetStamp are both MOTHER at two keys because a met week and a personal record became two different claims. The suite asserts the key list and that three keys resolve to two distinct strings, so a fourth shouted word fails.
nodes.norm_label: the shouted rows (three keys, two strings)

nodes.label: src/content/copy.test.ts (the copy suite)
nodes.rationale: Every rule is stated as the suite decides it, because that file is the half of the contract a commit cannot argue with. Where the suite decides nothing (R7, R11, the tone rule) the contract says so explicitly.

nodes.label: Rules left to review
nodes.rationale: R7, R11 and the round-three tone rule (the joke is about the app or the week, never about the user) are facts about aim and intent that no character scan can read out of a string.

nodes.label: The four unnumbered gates
nodes.rationale: No string may hold a URL because a string is not a place to put a link; every override key must exist in CopyKey; every override must carry the slots and literal digits its default carries and no others; and an override may rename an abort or a commit but never swap them (aborts button.cancel and button.dismiss, commits button.confirmSkip, button.confirmStart, button.wipeConfirm).

nodes.label: FORMAT frame
nodes.rationale: A string that interpolates a value is a function of its arguments rather than a template assembled at the call site, so a skin can reorder it. P8 converted twenty two template literals onto keys and the suite pins each to the clinical literal it replaced, byte for byte.

nodes.label: copy(key) / copyFor(skin, key)
nodes.rationale: A view calls copy(key) or copyFor(skin, key), never a literal, which is what makes the skin merge and the whole contract enforceable at one seam.

nodes.label: MAX_REASON_WORDS
nodes.rationale: Set to twelve in src/domain/training/progression.ts so the domain holds the same bound as R3 and a minted reason line cannot outrun the copy rule.

nodes.label: ADVICE_KEY map
nodes.rationale: Record<Enum, CopyKey> in src/ui/views/train/ExerciseCard.tsx, exhaustive by type, so a new enum member is a compile error rather than a lower-case model identifier on screen.

nodes.label: MODALITY_KEY map
nodes.rationale: Record<Enum, CopyKey> in src/ui/views/train/AddCustomExercise.tsx, exhaustive by type, keeping the modality enum off the screen under R11.

nodes.label: The missed-week screen
nodes.rationale: Three rows: advice.tapForSound and advice.tapToMute name the muted-autoplay state and give the clip its accessible name, and button.dismiss is the only control. Master plan decisions 10.9 and 10.2 rule out a play control and a per-week mute, and R13 stops a skin softening the one control that remains.

nodes.label: scripts/copy-wordcount.mjs
nodes.rationale: Produces the key, word and coverage counts per table, so the contract's numbers are generated rather than retyped.

nodes.label: scripts/limelight-side-by-side.mjs
nodes.rationale: Generates the review page from the tables so nothing in it is retyped and the contract does not restate a single row. Must be rerun after any table edit.

nodes.label: Limelight, beside the clinical default
nodes.rationale: A generated review page putting all 120 limelight rows beside the clinical default and the board column, one table per screen in tab order then the popups, with a key listed once under the first screen that renders it. The register is the reader's call, not the model's.

nodes.label: The three marks (keep, cut, rewrite)
nodes.rationale: keep ships the string as written, cut drops the row so the clinical string stands on that skin, and anything else written is the string that ships verbatim. A blank row ships as written. No second limelight pass runs before the marks come back.

nodes.label: The strings you named
nodes.rationale: advice.drinkToThirst reads hydrate or diedrate, status.prStamp and status.weekMetStamp read MOTHER, and button.startSession reads LET'S GO BABES. Frozen because the reviewer asked for them, but markable like any other row.

nodes.label: A skin changes words, never facts
nodes.rationale: Every slot is a number the app computed, so it survives every rewrite, and so do the units and the defined quantity names: 60 kg, 8 reps and beverage intake read the same on every skin. Binds whatever the reviewer writes, because it lives in the master plan rather than in anyone's taste.
nodes.norm_label: a skin changes words, never facts

nodes.label: A skin never jokes on a control whose misreading costs data
nodes.rationale: The wipe, the import, the legacy delete, the export, the save failures, the reminder states and the install steps have no rows on the page and will not get any; all 110 fall-through keys are named with a reason in src/content/copy.limelight.ts.
nodes.norm_label: a skin never jokes on a control whose misreading costs data

nodes.label: The 'same' marker in the board column
nodes.rationale: Means the departures board has no row for that key and the clinical string stands there, which is how the page shows the board's 37 rows against limelight's 120 without a second table.
nodes.norm_label: the 'same' marker in the board column

nodes.label: FixThisInjustice v2 Master Plan
nodes.rationale: Shared specification for every numbered plan in docs/plans/: turns a single-user 24-week console into a generic, phone-first, offline-capable PWA training companion. One static Vite/React/TypeScript PWA on GitHub Pages with all user data in one validated localStorage document, plus one Cloudflare Worker that only sends scheduled Web Push reminders.

nodes.label: Platform: stay a web PWA, replace the toolchain
nodes.rationale: Distribution by URL covers both phone platforms without an app store; Babel's own documentation says not to use @babel/standalone in production and the live site also ships React's development build. Platform floor iOS 18.4+ (Web Push needs an installed Home Screen app since 16.4; Screen Wake Lock in installed web apps fixed in 18.4) and Android with Chrome.
nodes.norm_label: platform: stay a web pwa, replace the toolchain

nodes.label: Capacitor native wrapper
nodes.rationale: Would give exact-time offline local notifications on both platforms, but an iOS build requires macOS plus Xcode and the Apple Developer Program (99 USD/yr) and this development machine is Linux. On Android 14 the exact-alarm permission is off by default and Google Play reserves the frictionless variant for alarm and calendar apps. Remains a possible later Android-only add-on because the web code is unchanged.

nodes.label: Expo / React Native rewrite
nodes.rationale: Carries the same iOS distribution barrier as Capacitor plus a full rewrite of working presentation code.

nodes.label: Reminders: Web Push sent by a Cloudflare Worker cron
nodes.rationale: No web API in 2026 schedules a future local notification without a server: Chrome ended Notification Triggers and Periodic Background Sync is Chromium-only with no time control. The client computes concrete reminder instants and uploads them; a Worker cron (* * * * *, free plan) sends due pushes within the free-plan budget of 100,000 requests/day, KV 100,000 reads and 1,000 writes/day, 5 cron triggers.
nodes.norm_label: reminders: web push sent by a cloudflare worker cron

nodes.label: Zero-server reminders: calendar export or ntfy
nodes.rationale: Calendar .ics alarm firing on import has insufficient evidence on both platforms, and ntfy needs a second app plus re-posting every 3 days. A one-time .ics export survives only as a courtesy in the Export view.
nodes.norm_label: zero-server reminders: calendar export or ntfy

nodes.label: Durable Object alarms instead of cron + KV
nodes.rationale: More precise, but adds bindings, migrations and per-object state for a handful of users; cron plus KV with an index key is one file. Revisit only if minute-level polling proves unreliable.
nodes.norm_label: durable object alarms instead of cron + kv

nodes.label: Push library: @pushforge/builder
nodes.rationale: Zero-dependency Web Crypto VAPID implementation built for Workers, MIT, released 2026-04. The alternative @block65/webcrypto-web-push was last published 2024-12 and is rejected as unmaintained.

nodes.label: State persistence: one localStorage key, Zod-validated, versioned
nodes.rationale: A year of training state is well under 1 MB, so a synchronous load at boot avoids a loading state and QuotaExceededError is handled explicitly with a blocking banner plus export. IndexedDB is used only for binary assets (the user-picked motivation video); IndexedDB for all state was rejected as async boot and transaction code for no capacity gain at this volume.
nodes.norm_label: state persistence: one localstorage key, zod-validated, versioned

nodes.label: State management: Zustand with selectors
nodes.rationale: Selector subscriptions stop the whole-tree re-render the monolithic useState caused (code review A41). Rejected: React Context plus useReducer (same re-render churn) and Redux Toolkit (weight without benefit at this size).

nodes.label: Dates: date-fns 4 + @date-fns/tz with explicit IANA zone
nodes.rationale: Every civil date is derived from the profile's IANA zone through TZDate and Date.prototype.toISOString on civil dates is banned by lint. Rejected: Temporal (polyfill size, uneven shipping) and Luxon (larger, overlapping).
nodes.norm_label: dates: date-fns 4 + @date-fns/tz with explicit iana zone

nodes.label: TypeScript 5.9 line
nodes.rationale: typescript@7 (the native compiler) is latest on npm but was not evaluated against Vite 8, Vitest 4 and typescript-eslint 8 here, so ^5.9.3 is pinned and revisited after the first release.

nodes.label: Clickjacking: confirmations, not CSP frame-ancestors
nodes.rationale: GitHub Pages cannot set response headers and MDN states frame-ancestors is not supported in the meta element, so every destructive action requires a typed confirmation plus a gated export first, and a JavaScript frame check hides the UI when framed. Corrects the security review's constraint 15.

nodes.label: Activity level has three members
nodes.rationale: Collapsed to the three verified FAO/WHO/UNU 2004 PAL bands (sedentary, moderate, vigorous). Rejected: five members with two unverified midpoint multipliers, because no invented midpoint may ship as a number.

nodes.label: Limelight skin ships selected; brat and stan retired
nodes.rationale: Skin ids are clinical, limelight and board, with limelight the shipped default at src/domain/schema.ts:511 so a document written before the field existed opens on the shipped look rather than a set it never chose. Rejected: keeping brat and stan as separate skins (ships E's blur, F's CC-BY emoji obligation and the arithmetic the user rejected) and the id cunty (no-slurs rule on identifiers).
nodes.norm_label: limelight skin ships selected; brat and stan retired

nodes.label: Brat and stan as separate skins
nodes.rationale: Rejected alternative to the round-three merge: shipping them separately would carry E's blur, F's CC-BY emoji attribution obligation and the arithmetic the user rejected, three times over.
nodes.norm_label: brat and stan as separate skins

nodes.label: Readiness screen in own wording, modelled on PAR-Q+
nodes.rationale: The official PAR-Q+ form is all rights reserved and its 2011 paper has no resolvable DOI, so the screen asks the same seven screening domains in the project's own words, states it is not medical advice and names PAR-Q+ as the model. Rejected: reproducing the form verbatim, which requires written permission from the copyright holder that was not obtained. A positive answer sets Profile.readiness.flagged and shows a physician-consult notice at every session start.
nodes.norm_label: readiness screen in own wording, modelled on par-q+

nodes.label: Motivation modal has one Dismiss control
nodes.rationale: Rejected: a second 'not this week' control that the contract could not make behave differently without a new field. The single Dismiss sets lastShownForWeek, lastShownAt and WeeklyReview.missHandled together.
nodes.norm_label: motivation modal has one dismiss control

nodes.label: Motivation miss window of 14 days
nodes.rationale: pendingMotivation returns only the most recent unhandled missed week whose close (midnight ending its Sunday in the profile's timezone) lies within MOTIVATION_MISS_WINDOW_DAYS = 14 of now. Without the bound a back-dated setPlan makes closeWeeks back-fill up to MAX_WEEKS_EVALUATED = 520 weeks, each an individual popup. Rejected: marking every historical miss handled at plan creation, because a plan back-dated by a fortnight contains real misses.

nodes.label: Reminder lead offset measured in elapsed time
nodes.rationale: A lead reminder sits at instantOf(date, slot.startTime, tz) minus leadMinutes*60000, a whole number of elapsed milliseconds, so the user always gets the notice the setting promises even though the clock-face gap differs across a DST transition. Rejected: subtracting the lead on the clock face then converting with instantOf, because a spring-forward gap reading resolves forward and delivers 30 minutes instead of 90, and an autumn overlap fires an hour early.
nodes.norm_label: reminder lead offset measured in elapsed time

nodes.label: Specimen PRNG: splitmix32 via seededRng
nodes.rationale: src/domain/fun/rng.ts exports seededRng as splitmix32 (bryc jshash/PRNGs.md, multipliers 0x85ebca6b and 0xc2b2ae35, shifts 15/13/16) seeded through xmur3, and every fun-mechanics draw goes through that one export. mulberry32 was replaced because it never emits about a third of the 32-bit values: over the first 2^27 outputs it repeats a 32-bit value 4,560,378 to 4,567,010 times across five seeds against 2,097,152 for an ideal uniform source and exactly zero for splitmix32, which is a bijection on its 32-bit state. The review's figure of 35,964,069 did not reproduce at any seed tested.

nodes.label: mulberry32 PRNG
nodes.rationale: Shipped first in src/domain/fun/rng.ts and replaced: its author records that it never emits about a third of the 32-bit values, and the repeat measurement bears that out. Keeping it on the grounds that the plan named it and the rarity split is only asserted to two decimal places was rejected, because carrying a known defect for the sake of a plan sentence is the wrong trade.

nodes.label: Specimen draw keyed by set ordinal
nodes.rationale: The draw uses ordinal = totalSetsLogged read after the increment, deleteSet decrements the counter, and the card an ordinal produced is recorded in acquiredByOrdinal so one ordinal can yield at most one card ever. A reused ordinal alone does not close the farm because the second roll runs against an inventory that already owns the first card, making log-look-delete-relog a working reroll. Rejected: a monotonic never-decrementing counter, which makes every fake-log-and-delete a fresh roll and inflates totalSetsLogged away from the real set count (code review A47).
nodes.norm_label: specimen draw keyed by set ordinal

nodes.label: Motivation clip: muted autoplay, tap to unmute
nodes.rationale: The clip autoplays muted with playsinline and loop, carries no transport controls, and a tap on the clip itself unmutes it with the hint advice.tapForSound. WebKit's iOS policy permits a muted inline element to start without a gesture, so the required gesture is spent on the element rather than an extra control the single-Dismiss decision removed. Rejected: the P6 plan's no-autoplay Play button, and an unmuted first attempt with a muted retry, because the latter makes the opening volume depend on the device.
nodes.norm_label: motivation clip: muted autoplay, tap to unmute

nodes.label: Media formats: MP4/H.264/AAC and .m4a or MP3
nodes.rationale: Every published media asset ships as one universal file (AAC in .m4a or MP3 for sound effects, H.264 plus AAC in .mp4 for video) with any smaller alternate beside it, never in place of it, because Safari is the browser this PWA is most likely installed under: MDN marks Vorbis and WebM unsupported there and contradicts itself on Opus. Rejected: shipping .ogg or WebM alone, because the asset is then silent on the platform that matters most and the failure is inaudible; check-sfx-size.sh and check-media-size.sh enforce the sibling rule.
nodes.norm_label: media formats: mp4/h.264/aac and .m4a or mp3

nodes.label: Global constraints (section 3)
nodes.rationale: Copied into every numbered plan: version floors, strict TypeScript with noUncheckedIndexedAccess and exactOptionalPropertyTypes, build-failing lint gates that confine toISOString to dates.ts and localStorage to persistence.ts, canonical units and sign conventions, ISO-Monday LocalDate in the profile zone, the CSP meta policy, the personal-data grep, feature-detection-only platform detection, the fti.v3 storage contract, gated destructive actions, Vitest requirements, the copy contract and the skin rules.

nodes.label: Canonical units and sign conventions
nodes.rationale: Storage is always canonical: mass kg, volume mL, duration s, instants epoch ms UTC, distance m, energy kcal, protein g, with 1 lb = 0.45359237 kg and 1 US fl oz = 29.5735295625 mL exactly. Display unit is a profile property applied only in units.ts. A logged load is never altered for display; only suggested loads are quantised, rounding down to the equipment step. Deltas are current minus reference, so a negative body-mass delta means loss and a negative weekly delta means sessions missed.

nodes.label: Content Security Policy meta tag
nodes.rationale: default-src 'self' with script-src 'self' and no inline script, eval or runtime JSX, enforced in CI by grepping dist/index.html. connect-src is replaced at build with the exact Worker origin from VITE_REMINDER_API and fails closed to 'self' when unset; frame-src is generated at build from src/config/videoInstances.ts so policy and video modal cannot drift.

nodes.label: Personal-data CI grep gate
nodes.rationale: No medication, biometric or location strings in tracked source; a git grep over the tree (exempting docs/review/, docs/plans/, REFERENCES.md and graphify-out/) must return nothing. One-character classes stop the pattern matching its own definition in the workflow, and the word boundary is load-bearing because an unanchored case-insensitive alternation also matches the same letters inside a base64 data URI.

nodes.label: Feature-detection-only platform detection
nodes.rationale: No code parses navigator.userAgent. The reminders panel decides from pushAvailability() (serviceWorker, PushManager, Notification) and isInstalledPwa() (the display-mode: standalone media query); a test defines a spying userAgent getter and asserts it is never called, because a user-agent string tells a user their browser cannot do something it can.

nodes.label: File structure after P8 (section 4)
nodes.rationale: The authoritative tree: Vite entry with CSP and referrer meta, injectManifest service worker, src/domain modules, the Zustand store, the copy and skin modules, the ui views, the worker package and the CI gate scripts. Corrected by the P9 pass to drop legacy/, TopBar, Nav, ProtocolsView, SkinRoot, useReducedMotion and skins/board/, none of which shipped.

nodes.label: Shared types contract (section 5)
nodes.rationale: The type contract every numbered plan shares; a plan may add fields only by editing this section first. Primitives carry their canonical unit in a comment, all Record<string, X[]> maps key on profileId unless stated, and sets keys on LoggedSet.id.

nodes.label: AppState root document (schemaVersion 3)
nodes.rationale: One persisted document holding profiles, availability, plans, cursors, pauses, assignments, sets, body mass, hydration, intake, weekly reviews, reminder settings, one device push subscription, motivation, specimens, capsules, custom exercises, notes and UiPrefs. Additive fields carry Zod defaults so CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION stays 3 across P1 to P8; no derived value is persisted.

nodes.label: Canonical exercise ids and direct-mover rule
nodes.rationale: Forty canonical exercise slugs the P2 library must use exactly, with muscleGroups counting 1.0 set for direct movers and secondaryMuscles 0.5 for dynamic assisting movers. A muscle is DIRECT when it is a prime mover through a large range under load; isometric stabilisers are neither. Equipment tiers nest bodyweight in dumbbells-only in full-gym, and the generator reports rear-delt and side-delt as maintenance-only on a bodyweight tier.
nodes.norm_label: canonical exercise ids and direct-mover rule

nodes.label: Deload cuts volume, not load
nodes.rationale: A deload PlanBlock sets setModifier 0.4 to 0.6 and keeps loadModifier at 1.0, never the reverse, per content peer review section 2.2 citing Bosquet 2007.

nodes.label: src/domain/types.ts
nodes.rationale: Holds every persisted and domain type, defined by section 5 of this master plan.

nodes.label: src/domain/schema.ts
nodes.rationale: Zod schemas mirroring types.ts, CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION and parseState(); every load, import and paste passes AppStateSchema.safeParse. Line 511 holds the skin enum defaulting to limelight and line 539 the hotkeys default.

nodes.label: src/domain/units.ts
nodes.rationale: The only module that applies the display unit: displayLoad, toStoredLoad, displayMass, toStoredMass, achievableLoad, stepFor, formatLoad, formatMass, formatVolume and UNIT_LABEL, with property tests over x in [0, 500] asserting round-trip within 0.05 + 1e-9.

nodes.label: achievableLoad equipment-grid quantisation
nodes.rationale: Largest grid point at or below the target: q = targetKg/stepKg, n = floor(q + 1e-9), and when |q - n| < 1e-9 the target is returned unchanged because re-multiplying n by stepKg reintroduces float error (28 x 2.2679618500000003 is not 63.5029318). A step of zero or NaN means no quantisation.

nodes.label: src/domain/dates.ts
nodes.rationale: The sole producer of LocalDate. instantOf computes only from tzOffset candidates so the result is invariant under the process zone, resolving gaps forward and overlaps to the earlier instant, matching Temporal's compatible disambiguation. addDays and daysBetween work on the calendar triple on the UTC line so DST cannot shift them. Tests run under four zones across both DST transitions.

nodes.label: src/domain/nutrition.ts
nodes.rationale: computeTargets throws RangeError outside the validated adult domain and returns a basis object naming the RMR equation, activity factor and the rules behind the protein, deficit and rate figures. targetKcal and expectedRateKgPerWeek are computed independently because no verified kcal-to-mass coefficient exists. Initial fat-loss cut is 10 % of TDEE, the band floor, because the band-floor activity factor already biases downward.

nodes.label: restSFor single rest-interval table
nodes.rationale: One table in src/domain/plan/library.ts: compound at 6 reps or fewer gets 180 s, compound at 6 to 12 gets 120 s, isolation loadClass gets 90 s (content review section 9). P4's defaultRestS delegates to it rather than redefining it, and it is never stratified by machine versus free weight, for which the review found insufficient evidence.

nodes.label: src/domain/schedule (cursor.ts, calendar.ts, weekly.ts)
nodes.rationale: Calendar-free plan progression: the cursor advances only on complete or skip and both are no-ops on a terminal assignment, at most one non-terminal assignment exists per profile, a paused day materialises no new assignment, assignToday preserves the weekly label multiset, and closeWeeks evaluates every ended ISO week with no review. Known limitation: target is the current weeklySessionTarget because no target history is stored.

nodes.label: src/domain/training/restTimer.ts
nodes.rationale: Rest is stored as absolute startedAt and endsAt instants and remainingS is recomputed from endsAt, never decremented, so backgrounding yields 0 rather than a frozen count. The timer lives in a non-persisted slice mirrored to sessionStorage, holds a Screen Wake Lock, unlocks an AudioContext on the start tap and posts a service-worker notification when hidden.

nodes.label: src/domain/training/progression.ts
nodes.rationale: suggestedProgression returns ProgressionAdvice whose reason is the user-facing line carrying no arithmetic and whose why renders only inside the 'why?' disclosure. e1RM uses Epley, load x (1 + reps/30), for 10 reps or fewer.

nodes.label: Double progression with percentage increment and equipment guard
nodes.rationale: Hold load until every prescribed set of the last session reached prescription.hi, then target p x L with p = 0.05 for lower-compound and 0.025 otherwise, rounded DOWN to the equipment grid and floored at one whole step, never up. The floor is why the applied percentage can exceed p: at 140 lb with p = 0.025 the 3.5 lb target rounds to nothing on a 5 lb grid, so one step ships at 3.57 %. If step/L exceeds 0.10 the advice is extend-reps (hi + 2) instead of added load. History is ordered by (assignmentDate, setNumber), never by wall-clock timestamp alone.
nodes.norm_label: double progression with percentage increment and equipment guard

nodes.label: src/domain/training/hydration.ts
nodes.rationale: No fixed between-set volume ships. preSessionMass takes the latest weigh-in at or before startedAt within PRE_SESSION_MASS_WINDOW_MS, bodyMassLossFraction is (pre - post)/pre and exceedsDehydrationThreshold fires above 2 %. dailyBeverageTargetML is re-exported from nutrition.ts. The 1.5 L per kg lost replacement figure is a paraphrase in the review and must not ship as a number.

nodes.label: HydrationCue as a copy key, not a sentence
nodes.rationale: The domain names the line and the view resolves it through the active skin: HYDRATION_COPY_KEY maps session-check, daily-shortfall and post-session-weigh to advice.drinkToThirst, advice.beverageShortfall and advice.logPostSessionMass, and the shortfall key is a template that must not be resolved bare. session-check fires at most once per 20 min of an active session; daily-shortfall after 18:00 local when volume is under half the daily target.
nodes.norm_label: hydrationcue as a copy key, not a sentence

nodes.label: src/domain/reminders/instants.ts
nodes.rationale: Builds the reminder instants and the push title and body, which are deliberately not skinnable because a notification is composed for a device that may render it while no app window, and therefore no skin preference, is loaded. scheduleHash gives stable change detection.

nodes.label: computeReminderInstants horizon clamp
nodes.rationale: For each projected calendar day with a slot and no pause it emits one day-of instant and one per lead offset, skips past instants, and clamps the horizon to now + 21 d in MILLISECONDS because 21 calendar days across a fall-back exceed 21 d elapsed and would make the Worker reject the whole upload.

nodes.label: src/domain/reminders/client.ts
nodes.rationale: subscribe(), syncSchedule() and unsubscribe(), plus pushAvailability(), isPushSupported() and isInstalledPwa(). The planned src/domain/reminders/platform.ts never existed and isIos()/isIosUserAgent() were dropped: the panel decides from the three states pushAvailability() returns.

nodes.label: Worker HTTP contract
nodes.rationale: JSON with CORS restricted to the Pages origin. PUT /v1/devices/{id} creates on first call and later calls must present the same secret or get 403; limits are 200 reminders and an at within [now - 1 h, now + 21 d]. DELETE needs a bearer secret. GET /v1/health echoes the VAPID public key so a key mismatch is a one-command check. The Worker stores no names and no body data.

nodes.label: Cron due-selection and send dedupe
nodes.rationale: Every minute the cron reads the KV device index and sends each reminder with at <= now, at > now - 15 min and key not already in the record's sent map; any 2xx counts as sent and the sent map is carried across client re-syncs and pruned past 24 h. A 404 or 410 from the push service deletes the record and removes the id from the index.

nodes.label: worker/src/index.ts
nodes.rationale: Fetch handler for PUT/DELETE /v1/devices/:id and GET /v1/health, plus the scheduled handler.

nodes.label: worker/src/schedule.ts
nodes.rationale: Pure, tested due-selection and dedupe logic, kept out of the fetch handler so the cron rules can be tested without miniflare.

nodes.label: worker/src/push.ts
nodes.rationale: Thin wrapper around the pushforge send call, so the VAPID library is reachable from one place.

nodes.label: pendingMotivation trigger
nodes.rationale: Returns the missed week that should raise the motivation popup. The profile is in the Pick because a week's close is midnight ending its Sunday IN THE PROFILE'S ZONE, and now is in the signature because a window needs a clock reading. Superseded by decision 10.5, which bounds the window at 14 days.

nodes.label: src/domain/motivation/trigger.ts and assets.ts
nodes.rationale: Missed-week trigger plus the idb-backed custom video: the blob is stored as an ArrayBuffer and rebuilt at read because a Blob put into IndexedDB under jsdom degrades to {} silently. MAX_VIDEO_BYTES is 150 MiB.

nodes.label: src/store/index.ts (AppActions)
nodes.rationale: The Zustand store and every action, extended per plan. Refused transitions land on status.lastActionError while defects rethrow: addCustomExercise and addBonusExercise throw on a colliding or unknown id because a duplicate id is a defect, not a user action the store can report. Callers own the clock throughout, so undoAvailable reads it as a parameter.

nodes.label: src/store/persistence.ts
nodes.rationale: The only localStorage user, owning the single key fti.v3. On a failed safeParse it keeps the last known-good state in memory, shows the error and offers export; QuotaExceededError raises a non-modal persistent banner so Export stays reachable. The store is the only writer, so persistence never races it, and import goes through replaceState.

nodes.label: src/domain/fun/rng.ts (seededRng)
nodes.rationale: The single randomness export for the fun mechanics, so replacing the algorithm later is one assignment and no call site moves. Math.random appears nowhere in the draw path.

nodes.label: src/domain/fun/specimens.ts
nodes.rationale: drawSpecimenForLoggedSet returns the card already recorded against an ordinal instead of rolling again, and declares OrdinalKeyedInventory until acquiredByOrdinal moves into SpecimenInventory and its Zod schema.

nodes.label: src/content/copy.ts and the skin copy tables
nodes.rationale: CopyKey union, DEFAULT_COPY as the clinical base, FORMAT frames, and copy.limelight.ts and copy.board.ts merged over the default. Views resolve through useCopy(), never the static copy(), or a tab strip reads the default table while the palette beside it reads the skin.
nodes.norm_label: src/content/copy.ts and the skin copy tables

nodes.label: src/skins/skinContext.tsx
nodes.rationale: Reads ui.skin, sets data-skin on the html element and provides useSkin(); there is no SkinRoot component and every skin's tokens live in [data-skin] blocks inside src/ui/styles/tokens.css.

nodes.label: Skin system
nodes.rationale: A skin is a token set, a copy table merged over the clinical base, an optional icon set and optional sound effects, selected by UiPrefs.skin. Skins may use camp, profanity and slang, but never slurs, body-shaming or food morality, and they never alter a number, a unit or the meaning of a plan-altering control: button.extendRest stays '+30 s' in every table because the SI Brochure gives S to the siemens.

nodes.label: Copy contract
nodes.rationale: Concise, honest strings with no dashes as sentence connectors, no emoji, no hedging and no exclamation marks; buttons at most 3 words, hero lines 8, advice lines 12. The arithmetic behind a value is not shown inline but lives behind a 'why?' disclosure and appears only when the user must act differently because of it. Terminology uses the defined quantity, never a colloquial stand-in.

nodes.label: src/config/videoInstances.ts
nodes.rationale: The single source of the Invidious host list, ported from the legacy INSTANCES list, from which frame-src is generated at build so the policy and the video modal can never drift. Iframes carry sandbox='allow-scripts allow-same-origin' and referrerPolicy='no-referrer'.

nodes.label: Verification gates (section 7)
nodes.rationale: One numeric pass criterion per plan, stated before the work: exact unit products, a 168-day span in four zones, hostile-input schema rejection, nutrition reproduced to 1 kcal and 1 g, a 540-cell generator sweep, an unchanged cursor over a 60-day advance, a backgrounded timer reading zero, a reminder sent exactly once across 30 cron ticks, one popup per missed week, and rarity proportions within 2 percentage points over 10,000 draws.

nodes.label: Amendment log (section 10)
nodes.rationale: Records every amendment requested by P1 to P8 and the decisions taken on them, plus the execution rule that plans run in order P1 to P8 and a later plan's step that duplicates an earlier definition is verified and skipped rather than repeated.

nodes.label: P7 close-out (2026-09-02)
nodes.rationale: Documentation, legacy deletion and CI gates done; the cutover itself was not executed because this clone has no git remote. Gates ran in a detached worktree so a second agent's in-flight edits could not mask a failure: 2267 tests across 114 files pass. Step 4's clean grep for 'legacy/' was abandoned because eleven files cite legacy paths as the provenance of a ported value and the citation is worth more than a clean grep. The graph regeneration is partial and says so in graphify-out/cost.json.

nodes.label: P8 close-out (2026-09-02)
nodes.rationale: Four batches A to D, each changing a stated contract: UiPrefs gains a persisted hotkeys switch because WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.4 requires an off switch for character-key shortcuts (and aria-keyshortcuts must not outlive the binding); status.prStamp splits into a record and a week-met key; seventeen unrendered copy keys were retired; nine FORMAT frames stopped assembling sentences from template literals, which had printed clinical English under every skin; and releaseAudio suspends rather than closes the shared context when sounds are on, because closing it mid-clip locked every later effect.

nodes.label: P9 documentation pass (2026-09-02)
nodes.rationale: Corrects this document wherever it states a contract the tree contradicts: sections 3 to 7 are contracts so those corrections replace text, while the amendment log only gains entries.
