Adds the platform-detection rule to the constraints every plan copies, drops the paths that never shipped from section 4, corrects the skin default, and records that the increment is floored at one whole step rather than rounded up.

nodes.label: P1 Foundation plan
nodes.rationale: Vite/TS/PWA scaffold, lint gates, CSP, units, dates, ids, types, Zod schema, persistence with quota handling, Zustand store skeleton, error boundary above the store, CI build and deploy workflow, legacy tree moved and scrubbed.

nodes.label: P2 Profile, nutrition and plan generator
nodes.rationale: Profile types, nutrition engine with cited equations, exercise library, split templates, plan generator, setup wizard including the pre-participation readiness screen, targets display and the daily kcal/protein check-in.
nodes.norm_label: p2 profile, nutrition and plan generator

nodes.label: P3 Calendar and cursor
nodes.rationale: Availability, plan cursor, assignments, pause and resume, pick-today with reshuffle, weekly review evaluation, and the Today and Plan views.

nodes.label: P4 Training session
nodes.rationale: Train view: unit-aware set logging, progression suggestion, coach line, rest timer on absolute timestamps with wake lock and audio unlock, hydration cue, form cues and the video modal.

nodes.label: P5 Reminders
nodes.rationale: The worker package with KV, cron and pushforge, client subscription and schedule sync, service-worker push handlers, reminder settings UI, an iOS install guide and the deploy runbook. parsePushPayload is total and the push handler has no early return, so a delivered push always shows a notification.

nodes.label: P6 Motivation video
nodes.rationale: Missed-week trigger, bundled and user-picked video, popup with tap-to-play and a once-per-week guard.

nodes.label: P7 Log, export, migration and cutover
nodes.rationale: Log view with charts, PRs and compliance, export and import with schema validation, the v2 to v3 migration with its unit prompt, the docs rewrite, legacy removal and the cutover checklist.
nodes.norm_label: p7 log, export, migration and cutover

nodes.label: P8 Fun mechanics and skins
nodes.rationale: Boot sequence, toast queue, specimen cards rewritten so only claims with verified citations ship (21 of 42 were WRONG and 17 PARTIALLY), corrected draw mechanic, Atlas, time capsule, spotlight, Konami, phase transition keyed to the cursor, and the skin system with its copy tables, tokens, icons and sounds.

nodes.label: P9 Prose pass
nodes.rationale: Final pass over every user-visible string and shipped document against the copy contract: rewrite, tighten, remove text that does not earn its place, with the user reviewing the diff. Written and executed last.

nodes.label: Security review 2026-09-01
nodes.rationale: 23 findings plus a constraints section. Its constraint 15 (frame-ancestors) is corrected by the CSP decision and its constraint 26 (personal-data grep list) is superseded by section 3. Import validation is its critical fix C1.

nodes.label: Code review 2026-09-01
nodes.rationale: 72 findings with a port/rewrite/drop table and a data-model proposal. A41 drove the Zustand decision, A47 the specimen counter, A26 stable custom-exercise ids, A60 bodyweight sets storing loadKg 0 rather than being falsy-dropped, and C.4 ids everywhere instead of composite string keys.

nodes.label: Content peer review 2026-09-01
nodes.rationale: The source of every equation, coefficient, activity factor, protein range, deficit rule, rest interval, split template and progression threshold, with verified citations reproduced as code comments. Nothing marked PARAPHRASE or COULD NOT VERIFY may appear as a number in the app, and a value absent from the report may not be hard-coded.

nodes.label: REFERENCES.md
nodes.rationale: Every external fact used in the plan, with the fetch method and the session id, so a reviewer asking where a number came from can tell primary text from a paraphrase.

nodes.label: PAR-Q+ (Warburton et al. 2011)
nodes.author: Warburton DER et al.
nodes.rationale: Health & Fitness Journal of Canada 4(2):3-23. Cited by title, journal, volume and pages with 'DOI not verified': Crossref and PubMed hold no record. The form itself is all rights reserved, so it is named as the model rather than reproduced.

nodes.label: FAO/WHO/UNU 2004 PAL bands
nodes.rationale: The three verified physical activity level bands the ActivityLevel type is restricted to: sedentary, moderate, vigorous.

nodes.label: ACSM 2007 exercise and fluid replacement
nodes.rationale: Replaces fluid by body-mass change and keeps in-session loss under 2 %, which is the threshold exceedsDehydrationThreshold applies. It is why no fixed between-set volume ships.

nodes.label: ACSM 2009 progression band
nodes.rationale: The 2 to 10 % load-increment band the double progression percentages sit inside.

nodes.label: IOM 2005 beverage share
nodes.rationale: Beverage share of daily water: male 3000 mL, female 2200 mL, explicitly NOT the 3.7 / 2.7 L total-water adequate intake.

nodes.label: Bosquet 2007 tapering
nodes.rationale: Cited by content review section 2.2 for the rule that a deload cuts volume and holds load.

nodes.label: bryc jshash/PRNGs.md
nodes.author: bryc
nodes.rationale: Source of both the splitmix32 variant used (multipliers 0x85ebca6b and 0xc2b2ae35, shifts 15/13/16), the xmur3 seeder, and the author's own record that mulberry32 never emits about a third of the 32-bit values.

nodes.label: WCAG 2.1 SC 2.1.4 character key shortcuts
nodes.rationale: Requires an off switch for a single-character shortcut set, which is why UiPrefs gains a persisted hotkeys field and the nav strip drops aria-keyshortcuts while it is false.

nodes.label: SI Brochure 9th edition Table 4
nodes.rationale: Gives S to the siemens, which is why board's shouted '+30 S' was a unit error and why a skin may change words but never a unit symbol.

nodes.label: MDN media containers and audio codecs pages
nodes.rationale: Marks Vorbis and WebM unsupported in Safari, and contradicts itself on Opus: the Containers page gives Ogg Opus to Safari 18.4 and later while the Audio codecs page still restricts Opus to a CAF container. The contradiction is what forces a universal MP4/M4A file rather than an alternate-only asset.
nodes.norm_label: mdn media containers and audio codecs pages

nodes.label: Round Three Plan — one merged skin
nodes.rationale: Visual-direction plan that merges design directions E (brat summer) and F (stan twitter) into a single skin; sections 1-7 written before any HTML, 8 records the agy critique, 9-12 written after the mockup was built and verified.
nodes.norm_label: round three plan — one merged skin

nodes.label: limelight (the merged skin)
nodes.rationale: Ship limelight as the single merged skin, opt-in and never default, retiring brat and stan as separate SkinId values so SkinId becomes clinical | limelight | board. The merge resolves both parents: F's marquee, quote-tweet and stamp give E the hierarchy events it lacked, while E's 10.91:1 lime field and size-only discipline give F a floor. Name chosen because 'lime' names E's ground and 'the limelight' names F's marquee and fandom gaze; it is also one copy table and one token set instead of round two's three.

nodes.label: serve (rejected skin name)
nodes.rationale: Native to ballroom and stan register and describes what the app does, but collides with web-codebase vocabulary (service, server, serveStatic), and a persisted enum value must survive being read out of context in a JSON export.

nodes.label: flopera (rejected skin name)
nodes.rationale: Funniest candidate and the user's own phrase, but it names the skin after failure. The id appears in Settings, exports and bug reports without the joke's context, breaking the tone rule that the joke is never about the user in the one string that cannot be softened.

nodes.label: Vulgarity kept out of the skin id and Settings label
nodes.rationale: Master-plan §3 forbids slurs and whether 'cunty' is one is genuinely contested across dialects. Vulgarity is honoured everywhere else; only the id is excluded because it is the one string that arrives with no context. The user can overrule it as a one-line change.
nodes.norm_label: vulgarity kept out of the skin id and settings label

nodes.label: Direction E — brat summer
nodes.rationale: Round-two direction supplying the flat lime field, lowercase everything, stretched narrow Archivo, size-only hierarchy, the docked bar and the mascot. Rated best in set for gym legibility on the LED-mirroring argument.

nodes.label: Direction F — stan twitter
nodes.rationale: Round-two direction supplying the marquee, the quote-tweet card, the MOTHER stamp with sparkle fan, and hard offset shadows. Its aubergine ground, white body type, card rotation, Bungee face and Twemoji glyphs were all dropped in the merge.

nodes.label: Lime ground #8ACE00 (option i)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over F's aubergine on three grounds: black on lime is 10.91:1, the highest body contrast in the project and the property that won E the gym-legibility criterion; the constraint it creates (pink cannot be type) is productive rather than costly; and every F form survives the move with more contrast. Ratios computed with WCAG 2.1 relative luminance in scratchpad/contrast.py.

nodes.label: Aubergine ground #16041F (option ii, rejected)
nodes.rationale: F's palette, legible at 19.60:1 white and 17.01:1 acid, but legible in the way F already was; it would have discarded the light-ground LED-mirroring advantage that won E a criterion.

nodes.label: Pink is never type on lime
nodes.rationale: #FF5FCB on #8ACE00 is 1.41:1, so pink is confined to fills, outlines and offset shadows and is type only inside a black panel (7.75:1). Stated absolutely with no size exception because a rule with a size exception is broken by the next person who resizes a heading, and a checker can enforce the absolute form.
nodes.norm_label: pink is never type on lime

nodes.label: #C4006B deep pink (rejected)
nodes.rationale: At 3.06:1 it would clear the large-text 3:1 threshold, so it is legal only with a size exception. Rejected to keep the palette rule absolute; #9E0050 at 4.25:1, the darkest still-pink pink, still fails 4.5:1.

nodes.label: #4A002E second ink on lime (computed, rejected)
nodes.rationale: The agy critique's concrete alternative computes at 8.20:1 and would be legal as type. Rejected on design grounds, not contrast grounds: a third ink undoes E's size-only hierarchy, and at 13 px it reads as nearly the accent pink, inviting a meaning that is not there. Recorded as the value to use if a second ink is ever genuinely needed.

nodes.label: The marquee
nodes.rationale: The user's stated favourite, inherited from F and improved four ways: it inverts to the single black strip on a light page, it becomes a real 44 px button that pauses while pressed with touch-action pan-y, it hosts the icon set, and its first item is the designated one shown under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Pausing is what makes it information rather than decoration.

nodes.label: The quote-tweet card
nodes.rationale: Round two's best single idea: last week's number embedded inside this week's remark, a week-over-week comparison in a shape no other visual culture produces. Re-grounded from a dark inset box to a black-ruled inset on lime.

nodes.label: The MOTHER rubber-stamp moment
nodes.rationale: Named by the user as enjoyed immensely and kept whole: scales 2.4 to 1.0 and rotates -14° to -6° over 700 ms with twelve sparkle icons fanning at 240 ms. The only rotated element in the skin, and the twelve Twemoji sparkles were replaced by icons from the generated set.

nodes.label: The hard-shadow snap
nodes.rationale: Replaces E's resample blur: the display line's pink offset shadow travels 12 px to 4 px while letter-spacing settles from .06em to -.045em over 260 ms, staggered 80 ms across at most three lines. Same sense of the type arriving at zero legibility cost, and the device now belongs to the stan parent rather than fighting it.

nodes.label: E's 0.4 px resample blur (dropped)
nodes.rationale: A soft edge beneath F's hard 4 px offset shadow reads as a rendering fault rather than a style, and it was already fenced in round two by 'no quantity is ever blurred' — the shape of a device costing more than it returns.

nodes.label: The motion budget
nodes.rationale: Exactly three orchestrated moments — the shadow snap, the stamp landing, the marquee — and nothing else moves; each has a defined prefers-reduced-motion: reduce fallback that renders the final state.

nodes.label: No quantity is ever animated, blurred or faded
nodes.rationale: Kept verbatim from round two. The rest clock ticks because it is a clock and does not transition; this is a data-integrity rule wearing a motion rule's clothes.
nodes.norm_label: no quantity is ever animated, blurred or faded

nodes.label: The copy contract
nodes.rationale: Buttons ≤ 3 words, hero lines ≤ 8, advice ≤ 12; no em-dashes and no emoji in any user-facing string; numbers, units and control semantics are never skinned and print exactly as src/domain/units.ts produced them; camp and profanity allowed, no slurs, no body-shaming, no food morality.

nodes.label: No explanatory arithmetic on any screen
nodes.rationale: Added from the user's complaint about verbosity: no percentages, plate-rounding steps, delta formulas or storage-unit conversions. The two quoted specimen strings are deleted outright, becoming '140 lb. up 5. why?' and '2 of 4. flop era.' The storage-unit sentence leaves the training screen entirely rather than moving behind why?, since the canonical storage unit belongs in Export.
nodes.norm_label: no explanatory arithmetic on any screen

nodes.label: Justification versus instruction
nodes.rationale: The agy critique found the hole: the first draft banned arithmetic without distinguishing a justification from an instruction. A percentage, rounding step, delta formula or unit conversion explains a decision already made and is hidden; a load, rep count, rest duration or plate breakdown is a number the user must act on and stays on screen.

nodes.label: The why? disclosure
nodes.rationale: A details/summary element closed by default, the only place a reason appears, holding one sentence of ≤ 12 words such as 'all sets hit 8 last time.' Verified closed on load with a summary clearing 44 px.

nodes.label: The tone rule — the joke is about the app or the week, never the user
nodes.rationale: Established in round two and enforced structurally rather than by intention: the title may be camp, the body may not, and the illustration may not carry a verdict. Round two's finding on direction G was that a lever in a picture cannot be argued away by the words next to it.
nodes.norm_label: the tone rule — the joke is about the app or the week, never the user

nodes.label: The limelight copy table (21 keys)
nodes.rationale: Round two's sixteen keys plus five added this round (why_progression, session_done, pr_stamp, intervention_body, settings_skin). Five strings the user named are kept verbatim. Every entry checked against §3.1: longest button 3 words, longest hero 7, longest advice 9, no em-dashes, no emoji, no arithmetic.

nodes.label: plan_progress copy key
nodes.rationale: Changed from '10 served. 1 flop. 37 to go.' to '10 served. 1 skipped. 37 to go.' The critique's most important find: 'flop era' aims at a week, which the tone rule permits, but '1 flop' aims at one particular missed session that may carry a skipReason of illness or bereavement. A count is data; a count with a verdict attached to each item is the app judging the user. 'skipped' is also the word the data model uses (AssignmentStatus).

nodes.label: Three strings that shout
nodes.rationale: Everything is lowercase so that MOTHER, LET'S GO BABES and the marquee mean something in uppercase. Shouting is only legible against a quiet baseline, so the uppercase list is closed at three.

nodes.label: The sixteen-icon generated set
nodes.rationale: Generate all sixteen icons with agy rather than restyling an existing set. Mixing sources would put eight rescaled 24×24 MIT icons beside eight generated 32×32 ones, and the seam would fall exactly along the line between the boring icons and the funny ones; the rescale is lossy; and a restyle deep enough to hide both is more work than generating, still ships an MIT notice, and converges on the generated half anyway. One source, one grid, one palette, one licence, all own work.

nodes.label: Pixelarticons
nodes.rationale: MIT, 1 036 free SVG, true pixel art on a 24×24 grid. Rejected because 32/24 = 1.333 is a non-integer rescale that destroys the pixel grid, and because it has none of the camp vocabulary. Kept as the fallback for a single later icon, accepting the rescale and the MIT notice obligation.

nodes.label: Kenney 1-Bit Pack
nodes.rationale: CC0 1.0, 1 078 tiles, 16×16 — the only pixel set that lands on 32 exactly (2×). Rejected because it ships tilesheets and Tiled .tmx/.tsx only, with no named per-icon PNGs, and lacks droplet, pause, skip, stopwatch and megaphone, so it cannot cover even the utility half.

nodes.label: Kenney Game Icons
nodes.rationale: CC0 1.0, 105 smooth-vector icons; eliminated on medium alone, since the skin needs true pixel art.

nodes.label: Phosphor Icons
nodes.rationale: MIT, 1 512 icons across 6 weights on a 256-unit viewBox. Smooth vector, so eliminated on medium; it carries only two of the six camp glyphs (high-heel, martini), and redrawing those on a 32×32 grid is drawing an icon while inheriting an MIT notice.

nodes.label: Tabler Icons
nodes.rationale: MIT, 6 184 SVG at 24×24 with a 2 px stroke. Smooth vector, eliminated on medium; only glass-cocktail matches the camp vocabulary.

nodes.label: Twemoji glyphs (removed)
nodes.rationale: Direction F carried six inline Twemoji SVG glyphs and their CC-BY attribution obligation. All six are gone along with every emoji character in the file, per the user's explicit instruction.

nodes.label: 32 px identifiability check
nodes.rationale: Stated before generating: an icon passes if its silhouette is identifiable at true 32 px on the lime ground without a label beside it, else it is hand-authored as a pixel grid. Result 16 of 16 passed, verified by rendering contact sheets at 1× and 4× and looking at them; judged by eye, not by grid analysis.

nodes.label: Icon slicing, downscale and palette-snap pipeline
nodes.rationale: One 4×4 sheet rather than sixteen prompts, so stroke weight and palette are consistent; sliced by connected component rather than grid because five icons overflow their nominal 256 px cell; RGBA premultiplied before the area average and unpremultiplied after to stop a green fringe, then alpha thresholded at 110/255; palette snapped to seven opaque colours plus alpha, drawn from the mascot's own palette so icons and illustrations are provably the same drawn world.
nodes.norm_label: icon slicing, downscale and palette-snap pipeline

nodes.label: Fixed green-dominance background key
nodes.rationale: Fixed threshold G > R+40 ∧ G > B+80 ∧ G > 150. Found brittle: a regenerated sheet on a more yellow lime (165, 202, 47) has G − R = 37, so the whole background was classified as foreground and snapped to opaque grey, caught by looking at the output rather than by an exception. Kept only for the icon sheet because it produced the shipped files at background fraction 0.601.

nodes.label: Self-calibrating corner-median background key
nodes.rationale: Samples the four 16×16 corners, takes their median as the reference, masks every pixel within Euclidean distance 72, then asserts the background fraction lands between 0.25 and 0.90 so a silent failure throws instead of shipping. Measured fractions 0.709–0.763 across the four illustrations.

nodes.label: int16 palette-snap overflow bug
nodes.rationale: A squared channel difference reaches 255² = 65 025, overflowing signed 16-bit, so argmin selected on wrapped-negative distances and every pink fill snapped to black — the icons came out as photographic negatives. Nothing threw, nothing warned, file sizes looked plausible; found by rendering a contact sheet and looking at it. Now guarded with int32 arithmetic.

nodes.label: Derived panel icon variants
nodes.rationale: A black outline is invisible on a black panel, so rather than ship two drawings five icons (megaphone, sparkle, barbell, stopwatch, crown) remap #000000 to #8ACE00, giving a lime outline at 10.91:1 on black. The other eleven only appear on lime.

nodes.label: The silhouette is carried by the outline, never the fill
nodes.rationale: Pink on lime is 1.41:1 and could not carry a shape; black on lime is 10.91:1 and does. Fills are interior only, which is why the same icons survive both the lime ground and the inverted panels.
nodes.norm_label: the silhouette is carried by the outline, never the fill

nodes.label: The seventeenth-icon liability
nodes.rationale: The set is coherent because it came off one sheet in one generation, so adding a later icon means re-prompting the whole sheet or accepting visible style drift. The half of the critique's objection that is correct, accepted as a standing cost rather than solved.

nodes.label: The four mascot illustrations
nodes.rationale: Round two had one image; this round adds four (lifting, crowned, flopped, resting) generated from the same style paragraph and character description so they are one character in four poses rather than four similar blobs. All palette-snapped to 256 px, 2 645–4 023 B, far under the 300 kB ceiling; own work with no real person, artist, brand or existing character named in the prompts.

nodes.label: The mascot (round pink blob)
nodes.rationale: Established in round two as brat-mascot-128.png and inherited from E; its palette (#000000, #FCA3BE, #BB5F7B, #6D6D6D, #242424) is the palette the icons snap to. The 96 px corner instance was removed from Today because the screen carried the same character twice, so the round-two file is not inlined.

nodes.label: Resting mascot on the intervention screen
nodes.rationale: The flop illustration is the funniest pairing and the wrong one: a collapsed mascot shown to someone who has just missed two sessions is a joke about the user, so the flop goes on Week review where 'flop era' aims at seven days. Rest and collapse make different claims — recovery is legitimate versus you gave up. Recorded as the single highest-risk unverified judgement in the round; the named swap if a second reader disagrees is an active pose.
nodes.norm_label: resting mascot on the intervention screen

nodes.label: The sound specification
nodes.rationale: Master-plan §3 already allows a skin optional sound effects, and this is the first skin with a moment worth scoring. Four moments and no more, because a fifth turns a training app into a slot machine. Nothing is built: no audio was generated, auditioned, transcoded or shipped, and the Settings toggle is a drawing. Default off, because the failure mode is a phone shouting in a public gym.

nodes.label: sfx.session_done
nodes.rationale: Fires when the last set is logged and session_done ('ate.') renders; the one celebratory sound, a short rising figure of 1.2–2.0 s.

nodes.label: sfx.pr_stamp
nodes.rationale: Fires when a LoggedSet beats the previous best and the MOTHER stamp lands; a hard percussive stamp with a bright tail timed to the 700 ms landing.

nodes.label: sfx.rest_over
nodes.rationale: The only functional sound of the four: the rest countdown reaching zero is the one piece of information a screen cannot deliver when the phone is face-down on a bench. Must be audible in a noisy gym without sounding like an ignorable notification.

nodes.label: sfx.intervention
nodes.rationale: Fires when the missed-week modal opens; soft and low rather than a sting, because a triumphant noise over intervention_body would break the tone rule.

nodes.label: AudioContext unlock on the first gesture
nodes.rationale: One AudioContext unlocked by a one-time document pointerdown listener plus an explicit resume() on the Settings toggle, never on load. The first draft bound the unlock to the start_session tap, which was a real bug: a PWA resumed straight into a session in progress never passes that button, so sfx.rest_over would have failed silently on the one path where it does any work. All four buffers are decoded at unlock, never autoplayed, one-shot and suppressed when the tab is not visible.
nodes.norm_label: audiocontext unlock on the first gesture

nodes.label: AAC in .m4a, Opus alternate, never Ogg alone
nodes.rationale: Ogg Vorbis and Ogg Opus have no Safari support, so an Ogg-only asset is silent on every iPhone, the platform this PWA is most likely installed on. Every Kenney audio pack ships Ogg Vorbis only, which turns transcoding to AAC from a preference into a requirement. Size target under 60 kB per file and 240 kB for the set; not precached by the service worker.
nodes.norm_label: aac in .m4a, opus alternate, never ogg alone

nodes.label: Sonniss GDC bundles excluded
nodes.rationale: Frequently described as free to use but not CC0: the bundle licence is a proprietary royalty-free agreement forbidding supplying the sounds onward as sound effects, which a repository shipping its own sfx/ directory would be doing. Recorded so the mistake is not made later.

nodes.label: Kenney — Interface Sounds
nodes.rationale: CC0 1.0, attribution not required, 100 files. Best single match: confirmation_00* or bong_001 for session_done, open_00* for intervention, tick_00* for rest_over. A candidate to audition, not a selection.

nodes.label: Kenney — Digital Audio
nodes.rationale: CC0 1.0, 63 files including powerUp ×12; powerUp* is the candidate for pr_stamp.

nodes.label: Kenney — UI Audio
nodes.rationale: CC0 1.0, 52 clicks, rollovers and switches; too small and too click-like for these four moments, kept only as a fallback.

nodes.label: Freesound CC0 pool
nodes.rationale: CC0 1.0 per Freesound's own FAQ, attribution not required though authorship may not be claimed. Widest pool but needs auditioning and per-file licence checking.

nodes.label: OpenGameArt CC0 sound effects
nodes.rationale: CC0 1.0 (licence tid=4, art type Sound Effect tid=13), UI click and switch collections; third option behind the Kenney packs and Freesound.

nodes.label: MDN's Safari and Opus contradiction
nodes.rationale: MDN's Media container formats page says Safari 18.4+ added Opus and Vorbis in Ogg containers, while its Web audio codec guide still says Safari supports Opus only inside CAF. The plan does not resolve it: it treats Opus as an alternate source listed first and never as the only file, which is correct under either reading, and rests the rule on MDN's uncontradicted statement that AAC in MP4 is supported by all major browsers.

nodes.label: The six-criterion verification checker
nodes.rationale: Round-two headless-Chromium script (playwright-core) at 390 × 844, run twice at no-preference and reduce: viewport meta, no horizontal scroll, every control ≥ 44 px, WCAG 2.1 contrast per text node against the composited background, zero emoji characters, disclosures closed on load. Result: passes all six in both modes — 0 controls under 44 px, 319 text runs with 0 below threshold, 19 animations running versus 0 under reduce. Stated limitations: it measures declared colours rather than rendered pixels, walks text nodes only so the 3:1 non-text guideline is reasoned rather than measured, and cannot measure touch collision or real devices.

nodes.label: Zero-emoji grep check
nodes.rationale: grep -P over U+1F300–1FAFF, U+2600–27BF, U+FE0F, U+2190–21FF and U+2B00–2BFF must return no match in markup, CSS, comments and the copy table alike, because 'gone from the visible screens' is not the claim the user asked for. Returned 0 literal, 0 decodable entities and 0 em-dashes.

nodes.label: Screen 1 — Today
nodes.rationale: Marquee, lifting illustration, ep. 12 of 48, the setlist, the three plan-altering controls with real semantics in fine print, and LET'S GO BABES. The only screen where straightforward encouragement is safe.

nodes.label: Screen 2 — Train
nodes.rationale: Rest at 1:47 of 2:00 in an inverted panel, the MOTHER stamp with the twelve-sparkle fan and the crowned mascot, the progression line as '140 lb. up 5. why?' with the disclosure closed. Restructured after a screenshot showed the stamp falling below the dock: the redundant 52 px 'upper' line was removed and the rest clock cut from 88 px to 78 px.

nodes.label: Screen 3 — Week review
nodes.rationale: '2 of 4. flop era.' with −2, the flop illustration, the quote-tweet quoting last week's 4 of 4, the seven-day strip and four target rows on a shared 1.25× scale. This is where the flop picture belongs because the word aims at the week.

nodes.label: Screen 4 — The intervention
nodes.rationale: The missed-week modal over a dimmed Today: camp title, plain body ('the week flopped, not you. monday is the next slot.'), resting illustration, one dismiss control. The screen round two named in all four mockups and drew in none, and the screen where the tone rule is hardest to hold.

nodes.label: Screen 5 — Settings
nodes.rationale: The skin picker row with 'the limelight' selected and the sounds toggle off by default, placed on screen 5 so it is one tap away rather than buried. Nothing was added to UiPrefs; sounds is not a real preference yet.

nodes.label: The agy adversarial critique
nodes.rationale: One adversarial pass over §1–§7, asked seven specific questions and told not to summarise or compliment, logged in REFERENCES.md. It is a paraphrase from another model, treated as prompting rather than evidence, and changed the plan only where the change is independently defensible. It found one outright bug (the audio unlock) and one copy string breaking the plan's own rule (plan_progress).

nodes.label: Keeping E and F as separate shipping skins
nodes.rationale: The cautious option of shipping E, F and limelight as three skins was rejected because it answers a question the user did not ask, because two of the three would carry defects this round fixed (E's resample blur, F's Twemoji CC-BY obligation, the exposed arithmetic, '1 flop'), and because every skin is a standing copy-review cost. E and F stay in docs/design/round2/ as the record of where the merge came from.
nodes.norm_label: keeping e and f as separate shipping skins

nodes.label: Master plan §3 (skins)
nodes.rationale: Defines a skin as a token set, a copy table, an optional icon set and optional sound effects; sets the no-em-dash scope, the no-slurs rule, and excludes media from injectManifest precaching. Cited as binding by the copy contract and the sound spec.

nodes.label: REFERENCES.md source log
nodes.rationale: Every licence, count and grid size in the icon evaluation, every candidate sound source, the MDN pages and the agy critique are logged there with the method used to verify each — repo LICENSE files, git trees, licence text inside downloaded zips.

nodes.label: Archivo variable, one family at two widths
nodes.rationale: Inherited from E at wdth 62, wght 800. One family solves the merge problem because the skin needs the same face to be a 76 px shout and a 12.5 px footnote, which F's Bungee cannot do.
nodes.norm_label: archivo variable, one family at two widths

nodes.label: Bungee (dropped from F)
nodes.rationale: A signage face with no width axis and no usable small-size range, so it cannot carry both the display line and the footnote.

nodes.label: Card rotation (dropped from F)
nodes.rationale: On a flat lime field with black rules a ±1.0° tilt reads as printing misregistration rather than attitude, and it costs the clean edge that makes the flat field work. Rotation survives only on the stamp at −6°, where it is the point.

nodes.label: Archivo word-space collapse fix
nodes.rationale: At wdth 62–76 with negative letter-spacing the word space collapsed ('theintervention', 'reducemotion'). Fixed with per-class word-spacing from .06em to .18em scaled to how narrow each class sets wdth; no numeral class received it, because a quantity has no spaces and a rule that touches numbers is not a typography rule.

nodes.label: Plate breakdown specified but not built
nodes.rationale: The critique's proposal that why? carry what goes on the bar was declined as a copy change: src/domain/units.ts quantises suggested loads to Profile.equipmentSteps but nothing computes a per-side plate list, so shipping that string would mean a skin inventing a number. Recorded as a Train-screen feature for a later plan.
nodes.norm_label: plate breakdown specified but not built

nodes.label: P9 Prose and Documentation Pass
nodes.rationale: Thirty-task plan in three ordered layers: the copy tables gated by copy.test.ts, then the call sites still rendering hardcoded English twins, then the documents that describe both. No task changes a number, a unit, a quantity name or the meaning of a control.

nodes.label: Governing intent (the user's five sentences)
nodes.rationale: Five quoted user sentences outrank every rule in the plan; where a rule and a sentence disagree the sentence wins and the rule is amended in the same commit. Sentence 1 sets the word-count target, sentence 2 is the R9 test, sentence 3 freezes three strings, sentence 4 licenses the limelight register without overriding the no-slurs rule.

nodes.label: Copy contract R1 to R11
nodes.rationale: Binds every string: buttons at most 3 words, heroes 8, advice 12, banners 2 sentences, no em-dash or connector en-dash, no emoji, no hedging, no exclamation mark, arithmetic behind why?, R10 exemptions, defined quantity names. Word counts exclude numerals and unit tokens.

nodes.label: A skin changes words, never facts
nodes.rationale: Every {slot} the default carries is carried by every override row, and a literal digit appears in an override only where the default has the same digit. A number, a unit and a quantity name survive every rewrite, so a skin can only reach the words around them.
nodes.norm_label: a skin changes words, never facts

nodes.label: scripts/copy-wordcount.mjs word-count harness
nodes.rationale: Nothing in the repository measured a word count, so the instrument is built before the copy tasks that quote it. It uses Vite's Node API because vite is the only local package that loads a .ts module with unextensioned relative imports; esbuild is not installed, so an npx esbuild recipe would reach the network.

nodes.label: wordCount rule: numerals, slots and unit tokens are not words
nodes.rationale: The rule is reproduced in the harness rather than imported, because copy.test.ts is a test module. Keeping the two in step is a manual duty, and the TOTAL line is the tripwire that catches drift.
nodes.norm_label: wordcount rule: numerals, slots and unit tokens are not words

nodes.label: DEFAULT_COPY, the clinical table (src/content/copy.ts)
nodes.rationale: The union of record. 522 keys over 23 families; advice, status, why and label carry most of the words, and each family is one task.

nodes.label: LIMELIGHT_COPY override table (src/content/copy.limelight.ts)
nodes.rationale: A Partial<Record<CopyKey, string>> merged over the default per key; 105 rows over 522 keys, 20.1 per cent. An unlisted key falls through to the clinical string by design, so coverage is a choice per key rather than an obligation.

nodes.label: BOARD_COPY override table (src/content/copy.board.ts)
nodes.rationale: 29 rows over 522 keys, 5.6 per cent. Upper case throughout, the design's em-dash rendered as the colon R5 prescribes, and the met-week stamp reading ALL DEPARTED.

nodes.label: src/content/copy.test.ts, the mechanical copy gates
nodes.rationale: Decides R1 to R6, R8, the R10 exemptions, slot parity, digit parity, the three-key shout list and the abort-versus-commit rule. R7, R11 and the round-three tone rule stay with human review because they are judgements about meaning.

nodes.label: R9: arithmetic lives behind `why?`
nodes.rationale: Show a derivation inline only if the user must act differently because of it. Everything else moves behind disclosure.why, whose summary is the literal `why?` and whose body is exempt from R1 to R4, so nothing is lost by moving it.

nodes.label: R11: name the defined quantity
nodes.rationale: A colloquial stand-in is a defect and a correct name that reads oddly is not. weight is wrong for a load on a bar and for body mass, calories is wrong for kcal, water is wrong for beverage intake, and Load PR is forbidden where the shipped line says load personal record.

nodes.label: Slot and digit parity across the skin tables
nodes.rationale: Each override table must carry exactly the default's slots and exactly the default's digits, so renaming or dropping a slot in the default breaks in the limelight and board tables rather than silently at runtime.
nodes.norm_label: slot and digit parity across the skin tables

nodes.label: Limelight register: brat summer crossed with stan twitter
nodes.rationale: Camp, lower case, aimed at the week or at the app and never at the person reading it. Vulgarity is licensed by governing sentence 4 and bounded by master plan section 3: no slurs, no body-shaming, no food morality. The register itself is the user's call, not the model's.
nodes.norm_label: limelight register: brat summer crossed with stan twitter

nodes.label: Frozen strings: hydrate or diedrate, MOTHER, LET'S GO BABES
nodes.rationale: Named by the user in governing sentence 3 and asserted by name at copy.test.ts:289. Exactly three keys shout, carrying two distinct strings: button.startSession, status.prStamp and status.weekMetStamp; a fourth upper-case row fails the gate.
nodes.norm_label: frozen strings: hydrate or diedrate, mother, let's go babes

nodes.label: Limelight rule 4: no joke on a control whose misreading costs data
nodes.rationale: Every string fronting a wipe, an import, a legacy delete, an export or a save failure stays clinical in every skin. Most of the 81 Settings keys fall to this rule, and the vulgarity licence stacks with it rather than competing: a vulgar row on a destructive control still fails.
nodes.norm_label: limelight rule 4: no joke on a control whose misreading costs data

nodes.label: The board table stays sparse on purpose
nodes.rationale: A board row exists only where a real airport term names the thing. The setup wizard, the nutrition targets, the readiness screen, the migration wizard, the export view and the data section fall through to clinical by design, and the reason is recorded once at the head of the file.
nodes.norm_label: the board table stays sparse on purpose

nodes.label: Rejected: mirroring limelight's coverage in the board table
nodes.rationale: Matching limelight's 105 rows would mean inventing airport vocabulary for a hydration shortfall and a body-mass check-in. A board that says REFRESHMENT SERVICE IRREGULAR about water is a joke wearing a uniform, not a register.
nodes.norm_label: rejected: mirroring limelight's coverage in the board table

nodes.label: 22 hardcoded English twins in the app shell
nodes.rationale: App.tsx, UpdatePrompt.tsx and RootErrorBoundary.tsx render English byte-identical to 22 default keys that have never been read. Master plan section 3 says a view imports copy('button.startSession'), never a literal, so the conversion is a repoint rather than a rewrite; a literal that does not match its row is fixed in the table first.
nodes.norm_label: 22 hardcoded english twins in the app shell

nodes.label: RootErrorBoundary reads copy(key) directly, and gets the clinical string
nodes.rationale: It is a class component and cannot call a hook. That is correct rather than a compromise: the recovery screen renders when the store failed to hydrate, so no skin preference is loadable.
nodes.norm_label: rooterrorboundary reads copy(key) directly, and gets the clinical string

nodes.label: 48 copy keys with no reference outside their own definition
nodes.rationale: 22 are twins closed by Task 15, 11 are migration-wizard keys superseded by the advice.legacy* and button.legacy* names, 3 are design rows with a skin override and no renderer, and 12 have neither renderer nor twin. tsc -b is load-bearing here: CopyKey is a union, so a deleted member something still names is a compile error rather than a runtime blank.
nodes.norm_label: 48 copy keys with no reference outside their own definition

nodes.label: Three design rows kept rather than retired: status.planProgress, status.prReached, toast.setDeleted
nodes.rationale: Each carries a skin row and sits in the copy.test.ts REQUIRED list, and no component renders it. A design row that shipped its skin table but not its component is a component the design still wants, so the missing call site is recorded as a task rather than deleted as a leak.
nodes.norm_label: three design rows kept rather than retired: status.planprogress, status.prreached, toast.setdeleted

nodes.label: ICON_FOR_KEY entries with no SkinLabel call site
nodes.rationale: 16 mapped keys, 4 reachable. Every remaining entry must either have a SkinLabel call site or a comment naming the component that will place it; where the component draws the glyph itself, the map entry is dead and comes out with the reason recorded.
nodes.norm_label: icon_for_key entries with no skinlabel call site

nodes.label: Push text is built in instants.ts and is not skinnable
nodes.rationale: push.body has no call site. Wiring it through FORMAT would let a skin reach the lock screen; retiring it matches what shipped, because a notification arrives with no app chrome to place it. The Worker bounds the title at 100 characters, the body at 300 and the tag at 120.
nodes.norm_label: push text is built in instants.ts and is not skinnable

nodes.label: Decision: the copy contract carries no pasted key list
nodes.rationale: A key list copied into prose rots the moment a task appends a key, which is what happened between the P2 sweep and the P8 close-outs. The contract now states where the union lives and what binds it, R1 to R11 plus the four tests in copy.test.ts, and gives table counts instead of rows.
nodes.norm_label: decision: the copy contract carries no pasted key list

nodes.label: Decision: R10 names docs/RUNBOOK-reminders.md
nodes.rationale: R10's exemption pointed at worker/RUNBOOK.md, which does not exist. The P7 close-out records that the runbook was never moved and that README.md links the real path, so the rule text moves to the shipped location.

nodes.label: docs/RUNBOOK-reminders.md
nodes.rationale: R10 exempts the runbook from the length rules and does not exempt it from being accurate: every status string it quotes must appear verbatim in copy.ts, and the counts it claims must match the table.

nodes.label: docs/design/2026-09-02-limelight-side-by-side.md
nodes.rationale: One row per limelight key, both strings quoted byte for byte from the tables rather than retyped, and an empty verdict column. The pass stops here and hands over: the register is the user's decision, and every later task is independent of their answer.

nodes.label: Incident 2026-09-02: git commit --amend rewrote another agent's commit
nodes.rationale: An --amend rewrote commit ca5d972 into 0fa62cb and cost that agent a re-commit. 0fa62cb is still mislabelled, describing a toast fix over runbook content, and history was left as it is.
nodes.norm_label: incident 2026-09-02: git commit --amend rewrote another agent's commit

nodes.label: Incident 2: a stale-parent blob deleted the boot keys
nodes.rationale: Commit f7ceb3a committed a copy.ts blob built from a stale parent, deleting the boot keys, restored in 9d42e8d. The countermeasure is to build the blob from HEAD immediately before the write and to read git diff HEAD~1 HEAD for deletions you did not intend.
nodes.norm_label: incident 2: a stale-parent blob deleted the boot keys

nodes.label: Explicit pathspecs, never git add -A and never --amend
nodes.source_location: lines 51-58, repeated in every task's commit step
nodes.rationale: Two read-only reviewers and other agents hold edits in the same working tree, so a glob over test or view files would sweep their work into this commit. Every commit names its files, and each task re-states the rule at the point where a glob would be tempting.
nodes.norm_label: explicit pathspecs, never git add -a and never --amend

nodes.label: Decision 10.9: the motivation clip autoplays muted, tap to unmute
nodes.rationale: The clip carries playsinline, muted, autoplay and loop with no transport control. Decision 10.2 had already settled the dialog on one Dismiss control, and WebKit's iOS policy permits a muted inline element to start with no gesture, so the clip is running before the user decides whether to hear it. advice.tapForSound names that state while it holds.
nodes.norm_label: decision 10.9: the motivation clip autoplays muted, tap to unmute

nodes.label: P6 Task 4 draft: no autoplay and a Play button
nodes.rationale: The draft specified a modal that never autoplays and carries a Play button, and a MotivationModalProps block with two callbacks. What shipped is a muted autoplay with tap-to-unmute and one onDismiss; the difference is recorded as a decision rather than left to read as drift.
nodes.norm_label: p6 task 4 draft: no autoplay and a play button

nodes.label: Decisions 10.7 and 10.8: no ambient randomness in the specimen draw
nodes.rationale: attemptSpecimenDraw takes three arguments and reaches no ambient randomness; the draw goes through drawSpecimenForLoggedSet seeded from stored state, so a replay returns the card that ordinal already produced. The plans' rng parameter never existed in the shipped action.
nodes.norm_label: decisions 10.7 and 10.8: no ambient randomness in the specimen draw

nodes.label: Residual ledger, verified against the tree on 2026-09-02
nodes.rationale: 41 open items, each probed with git grep or sed before it earned a task, and 13 more recorded as closed by a later commit and dropped. A candidate with no probe does not become a task.
nodes.norm_label: residual ledger, verified against the tree on 2026-09-02

nodes.label: Baseline: 522 keys and 2175 words, measured 2026-09-02
nodes.rationale: The single number governing sentence 1 asked for, and the tripwire on the harness: any other total on the untouched tree means the script diverged from wordCount in copy.test.ts, and the script is wrong rather than the table.

nodes.label: status.remindersNeedReenable, the eighth status string
nodes.rationale: Added in 02dee88 and mapped from needs-reenable at ReminderSettingsPanel.tsx:44. The runbook claimed seven status strings; the table holds eight.

nodes.label: The push subscription is a bearer credential the export withholds
nodes.rationale: The reminder preference travels with an exported document and the subscription does not, so a restoring device holds enabled = true with no device. Nothing recovers on its own, so the panel names the device and the action instead of reporting a schedule that was never sent.
nodes.norm_label: the push subscription is a bearer credential the export withholds

nodes.label: Task 28 visual pass: no pixel has been measured
nodes.rationale: Every layout claim in the repository comes from jsdom, which renders no geometry, or from a design document. The marquee, week stamp, intervention CSS, Atlas grid, boot line width, Konami overlay, toast stack and safe-area insets are unverified. The pass must run from the installed app rather than a browser tab, because a tab has different safe-area insets and viewport units.
nodes.norm_label: task 28 visual pass: no pixel has been measured

nodes.label: Task 29: refresh the knowledge graph after the decision headers
nodes.rationale: The global instruction file requires graphify --update after a decision header changes, and the last regeneration was partial with an unsaved manifest, so 46 documents and images still read as changed. The checks are that every header reaches graph.json and that no node cites a deleted path.
nodes.norm_label: task 29: refresh the knowledge graph after the decision headers

nodes.label: 20-minute runtime cap on any run
nodes.rationale: The full suite takes about 3 min 25 s. graphify . --update is the only task that can approach the cap and is timed and interruptible; npm run test:tz is four full suites and is left to CI.

nodes.label: P9 close-out and its what-was-not-done list
nodes.rationale: Appended to master plan section 10, never edited into an existing entry. Every figure comes from a command run in that task, and a grep for unfilled angle brackets is a gate, because a placeholder left in a close-out is a false record. The omissions named are the unmeasured pixels, the unsettled limelight register, the unswept code-comment em-dashes, the missing monochrome badge icon, four untracked probe test files, the mislabelled 0fa62cb, the three unwired design rows, the unmachine-checked R7 and R11, and the unrun cutover.
nodes.norm_label: p9 close-out and its what-was-not-done list

nodes.label: FixThisInjustice training console
nodes.rationale: A static, account-free web app that builds a training programme from body data, goal, equipment and weekly availability and logs the sets actually done. Kept serverless so no training data leaves the device; the only server component is an optional Cloudflare Worker that sends session reminders and does nothing else.

nodes.label: Seven-tab console navigation
nodes.rationale: Today, Plan, Train, Targets, Log, Atlas and Settings. The tab list is declared once, in src/ui/nav/views.ts, so the strip cannot drift from the router. Export is reached from the data section of Settings rather than from the strip, and availability from the setup wizard, keeping the strip to the seven daily surfaces.

nodes.label: Three skins: clinical, limelight, board
nodes.rationale: A skin changes tokens, wording, icons and optional sounds and never a number, a unit or what a control does. That boundary keeps presentation swappable without putting a training or nutrition figure at risk. limelight is the shipped default.

nodes.label: iOS 18.4 platform floor
nodes.rationale: iPhone and iPad require iOS 18.4 or later, not 16.4 (the release that first gave installed web apps Web Push), because the Screen Wake Lock the app holds during a session stayed broken inside an installed web app until 18.4. src/ui/hooks/useWakeLock.ts records the reason.

nodes.label: Single storage key fti.v3, one writing module
nodes.rationale: Everything the app records lives under one key, fti.v3, and src/store/persistence.ts is the only module allowed to touch web storage. A lint rule in eslint.config.js fails the build if another module tries, so the single-writer rule is enforced mechanically rather than by convention.
nodes.norm_label: single storage key fti.v3, one writing module

nodes.label: Shared-origin exposure of a GitHub Pages project site
nodes.rationale: A Pages project site shares an origin with every other project published under the same account, so any page on that origin can read this app's storage. A custom domain or a dedicated user site closes it; until then, nothing untrusted may be published to the same account.
nodes.norm_label: shared-origin exposure of a github pages project site

nodes.label: No personal data in the repository
nodes.rationale: No medication, biometric or location string belongs in tracked source. Both workflows grep the tree for the forbidden identifiers and fail on a hit. docs/review/, docs/plans/ and REFERENCES.md are exempt because they discuss the terms, and graphify-out/ because it is a generated index of the other three.
nodes.norm_label: no personal data in the repository

nodes.label: One-way import from the old console
nodes.rationale: First launch offers a one-way import of the previous version's data. It asks the two units the old app never recorded, load unit and body-mass unit, because a wrong answer would rescale the whole history. The legacy JSON is downloadable before the import is kept, and old data is deleted only on an explicit user action.
nodes.norm_label: one-way import from the old console

nodes.label: Export-before-delete destructive gate
nodes.rationale: Settings offers a JSON backup of the whole document, a plain-text summary and an .ics of upcoming sessions. A destructive action is enabled only after an export has happened in the same dialog and then asks the user to type DELETE, because there is no server copy to restore from.

nodes.label: What leaves the device when reminders are on
nodes.rationale: Only two things leave the device, and only with reminders enabled: the push subscription the browser vendor issues, which identifies a browser install rather than a person, and the instants of the next sessions with the session label in the notification text. The data is not encrypted at rest, so anyone holding the unlocked phone can read it.
nodes.norm_label: what leaves the device when reminders are on

nodes.label: CI verify job
nodes.rationale: Runs on every push and pull request to main: media and sfx size gates, the emoji gate, the P7 legacy gate, npm ci, lint, typecheck, the four-time-zone suite, build, build hygiene, the CSP content check and the personal-data grep. The no-Node gates run before the install so an oversized clip fails in seconds rather than after a minute of npm ci.

nodes.label: CI worker job
nodes.rationale: The Worker is a separate npm package with its own lockfile, so it gets its own job rather than extra steps in verify. It is not linted: worker/ sits outside the root ESLint configuration, so tsc and Vitest are its gates.

nodes.label: P7 legacy-tree and superseded-document gate
nodes.rationale: git ls-files over the pathspec the P7 cutover deleted (legacy/, DEPLOY.md, PROJECT_SUMMARY.md, the console-*.jsx and prototype-*.html prototypes, sw.js, manifest.json, uploads, screenshots). A re-added legacy/ would ship the medication text the content review ordered removed, and a re-added DEPLOY.md would name a file set the build stopped producing. Tracked files only: an untracked copy on a developer's disk is not CI's business.

nodes.label: Build hygiene gates on dist/index.html
nodes.rationale: Four assertions on the built HTML: every <script> carries src= (the CSP is script-src 'self', so an inline script is dead code); no unpkg and no text/babel, which is how the legacy console loaded React and compiled JSX at runtime; the CSP meta tag survives, because GitHub Pages cannot set response headers and the meta tag is the only enforcement point; and the built frame-src matches its source of truth.

nodes.label: Six-host frame-src allowlist
nodes.rationale: Gate 4a compares the built frame-src against the host list build/cspPlugin.ts read from src/config/videoInstances.ts so policy and runtime list cannot drift; gate 4b compares that list against the six Invidious hosts master plan section 3 approved, so the frame allowlist cannot widen without a plan amendment.

nodes.label: Personal-health-data grep over the tracked tree
nodes.rationale: P7 widened the pathspec from src/ worker/ public/ index.html to the whole tracked tree, exempting docs/review/, docs/plans/, REFERENCES.md and graphify-out/. One-character classes stop the pattern matching its own definition. The \b anchor is load-bearing: unanchored and case-insensitive, the location identifier matched the same letters inside a base64 data URI in src/skins/limelight/icons.ts (commit 8511f21), failing on generated data rather than prose. Measured 2026-09-02, \b alone clears that false positive, so the two generated asset modules are now covered.
nodes.norm_label: personal-health-data grep over the tracked tree

nodes.label: Job-level VITE_REMINDER_API and VITE_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY
nodes.rationale: Declared at job level, not step level. VITE_REMINDER_API is read twice, by build/cspPlugin.ts during npm run build and by scripts/check-dist-csp.sh, which asserts the built connect-src names exactly that origin. Scoped to the Build step, the variable would be unset by the time the check runs and its assertion would pass without checking anything. An empty value is a valid build, because the reminder Worker is optional.

nodes.label: Pages deploy build job
nodes.rationale: Builds dist/ and uploads it as a Pages artifact, repeating CI's asset, copy, legacy, build-hygiene and grep gates. Lint, types and the four-zone suite are left to ci.yml, which runs in parallel on the same push.

nodes.label: GitHub Pages deployment job
nodes.rationale: actions/deploy-pages against the github-pages environment, gated on the build job. Concurrency group pages with cancel-in-progress false: one deployment at a time, and queued runs are not cancelled because a half-finished Pages deployment is worse than a slightly stale one.

nodes.label: Gates duplicated across independent workflows
nodes.rationale: The asset and content gates are repeated in deploy.yml rather than left to ci.yml because the two workflows are independent: a red ci.yml does not stop deploy.yml from publishing, so a gate that runs only in CI does not guard the live site.

nodes.label: Deploy cutover checklist
nodes.rationale: The one-off sequence that publishes the rewritten app: confirm the remote, set the Pages source, set the two repository variables, deploy the Worker before the site so the origin exists at build time, push, then verify the service worker registration and cache name. Every later deploy is a push to main and nothing else.

nodes.label: Pages source set to GitHub Actions
nodes.rationale: Without Source: GitHub Actions, actions/deploy-pages fails with 'Failed to create deployment (status: 404)' and nothing publishes. It is also the hardest step to undo, because switching the source retires the branch-based build that served the old console.
nodes.norm_label: pages source set to github actions

nodes.label: Site, Worker and data rollback
nodes.rationale: Re-running an earlier successful Deploy run republishes that commit because a re-run keeps the original GITHUB_SHA and GITHUB_REF; GitHub allows this for 30 days and 50 re-runs, after which a revert commit achieves the same. It restores an earlier Actions deployment only, not the branch-based old console, and the legacy storage keys survive the whole cutover.

nodes.label: Four conditions that open the import panel
nodes.rationale: src/ui/migration/MigrationGate.tsx opens the panel only when the legacy document fti.console.v2 is on the device, the decision is still pending, a profile exists (every migrated record is keyed by a profile id) and a plan exists (the migration matches legacy days against its sessions). The last two are why the offer usually appears on the second open, after the setup wizard. The load-unit question is never defaulted, because a wrong answer rescales the whole load history by the pound-to-kilogram factor.
nodes.norm_label: four conditions that open the import panel

nodes.label: readLegacyBundle export of the three legacy keys
nodes.rationale: readLegacyBundle in src/store/persistence.ts writes one bundle holding fti.console.v2, fti.plan.v1 and fti.video.instance as raw text. It is required at the delete rather than at the import, because the import writes nothing until the user types IMPORT and leaves the legacy keys untouched; ConfirmDestructive then enables the delete only after that download happened in the same dialog.
nodes.norm_label: readlegacybundle export of the three legacy keys

nodes.label: Shared origin risk carried deliberately
nodes.rationale: Security review M4 and master plan section 9 record that a Pages project site shares its github.io origin with every other project under the account, so this app's storage is reachable from any other page there. Accepted for the cutover rather than blocking it; a custom domain or a dedicated user site closes it.

nodes.label: Manual Cloudflare Worker deploy
nodes.rationale: Worker deploys are deliberately manual: a deploy touches a KV namespace holding live push subscriptions, so a person confirms each one. Neither workflow runs wrangler deploy and the repository holds no CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN. Sections 1 to 10 run once at setup, then section 7 alone whenever worker/src/ changes. Wrangler is installed only in worker/ (lockfile-pinned 4.128.0), so running it from the repository root would make npx fetch a different version.

nodes.label: REMINDERS KV namespace
nodes.rationale: Created with wrangler kv namespace create REMINDERS and pasted into worker/wrangler.toml over the REPLACE_WITH_KV_NAMESPACE_ID placeholder by hand rather than with --update-config, so the change is visible. It stores a random secret, a push subscription and the next three weeks of reminder instants per device, and an idx key indexing the devices; wrangler deploy fails loudly on an invalid id, so a surviving placeholder cannot reach production quietly.

nodes.label: VAPID key pair
nodes.rationale: Generated once with npx @pushforge/builder vapid. The public key goes to wrangler.toml [vars] and a GitHub repository variable; the private key goes in as the Worker secret VAPID_PRIVATE_JWK, pasted as a one-line JWK JSON object because worker/src/push.ts hands the string straight to the library. Regenerating invalidates every existing subscription, and a mismatched pair makes the push service accept every push and deliver none.

nodes.label: ALLOWED_ORIGIN exact-origin check
nodes.rationale: The exact scheme and host of the Pages site with no trailing slash and no path. worker/src/index.ts rejects any request whose Origin header differs and echoes the value as Access-Control-Allow-Origin, so a one-character mismatch turns every browser call into a 403. ADMIN_CONTACT is the RFC 8292 contact sent on every push.

nodes.label: The two GitHub repository variables
nodes.rationale: VITE_REMINDER_API and VITE_VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY are variables rather than secrets because both values are public by design: the browser calls the Worker URL and the push service is handed the public key. VITE_REMINDER_API must be a bare origin; build/cspPlugin.ts rejects a wildcard, a non-https scheme, userinfo credentials, and any path, query, fragment or trailing slash. The build fails closed to connect-src 'self'.

nodes.label: Workers free-plan budget arithmetic
nodes.rationale: At 1440 ticks a day, KV reads are 1440*(1+N) against a 100,000/day cap, giving N<=68; writes total about 70 a day in steady state against 1,000; deletes sustain at roughly 100/14 a day. Subrequests are the binding constraint at 50 per invocation, roughly N<=20 devices, so that is the number to watch rather than the daily quotas. Not verified: whether Cron Trigger invocations consume the 100,000 requests/day quota, though the Worker stays inside the cap either way.

nodes.label: Hourly index reconcile
nodes.rationale: The tick reconciles idx against the real key list only at minute 0 of the hour: 24 list requests a day, 2.4 percent of the 1,000 free-tier quota. Reconciling every tick would need 1,440 list requests and exceed the quota by 44 percent.

nodes.label: Inert-device reaper
nodes.rationale: Before the reaper, a device whose reminders had all fired was never pushed to, so the push service never answered 410 and nothing deleted it; the record cost 1,440 reads a day and held one of the 100 slots for the life of the namespace. The reaper deletes such a record on the hourly reconcile tick once it has gone INERT_DEVICE_TTL_MS (14 days) without a PUT, so N tracks devices still syncing and the budget holds over years rather than over the first fortnight.

nodes.label: pushAvailability() runtime capability check
nodes.rationale: One call in src/domain/reminders/client.ts returns ready, needs-install or unsupported by reading the runtime's features, never by parsing a user-agent string, so the app never tells a user their browser cannot do something it can. Installed-app detection uses the (display-mode: standalone) media query with a navigator.standalone fallback. needs-install shows the install guide and no toggle, because subscribing cannot succeed there.

nodes.label: Eight reminder status strings
nodes.rationale: The status.reminders* keys in src/content/copy.ts. Exactly one is shown at a time. The templated last string reports a wall clock in the profile's timezone, never UTC and never the phone's zone, so the reported time does not move when the user travels.

nodes.label: needs-reenable after a restore
nodes.rationale: The reminder preference travels with an exported document but the push subscription does not, because it is a bearer credential the export deliberately withholds. On the restoring device nothing recovers on its own, so the panel names the device and the action through status.remindersNeedReenable.

nodes.label: Install-before-enable on iOS
nodes.rationale: Safari delivers Web Push only to a web app installed on the Home Screen, from iOS 16.4. The app nevertheless floors at iOS 18.4 for a separate reason, the Screen Wake Lock the training screen holds. Android Chrome receives push in a tab, so installing is optional there; the in-app guide still shows both halves because the user reached it from a runtime that reported needs-install.

nodes.label: Phone smoke test for reminders
nodes.rationale: Add an availability slot five minutes out, include a 30-minute lead time, confirm the last-sent time updates, watch wrangler tail for devices=1, lock the phone, and check the notification arrives once within a minute and opens the Today view. The outcome is recorded in the section 16 log so a later regression has a baseline.

nodes.label: wrangler rollback of the Worker
nodes.rationale: npx wrangler rollback from worker/, omitting the version id to return to the previous version. Reminders stop arriving and nothing else in the app is affected, because every other feature runs offline against local state.

nodes.label: Clearing a device record by hand
nodes.rationale: wrangler kv key list/delete with the dev: prefix, which keeps idx out of the listing. Neither --local nor --remote defaults in 4.128.0 and the two conflict, so name the one you mean. Leave idx alone: the next tick drops the id in a write it was already making, and editing the index by hand risks dropping a device a concurrent PUT just added. Deletion does not ban the device, since a PUT for an unknown id is a create.
nodes.norm_label: clearing a device record by hand

nodes.label: Bundled motivation clip
nodes.rationale: One clip at public/media/motivation.mp4, played after an ISO week closes below its session target. The name is fixed and nothing scans the directory, so a file under any other name is published but never played. Shipping no clip is a supported state; public/media/ holds only .gitkeep today.

nodes.label: H.264 and AAC in MP4 for every published video
nodes.rationale: Master plan decision 10.10. The app ships one clip and one src rather than a list of <source> elements, so the single file has to be the format that plays everywhere. MDN marks both Vorbis and WebM unsupported in Safari, the browser this app is most likely installed under, so an Ogg-only or WebM-only asset is silent on every iPhone. A smaller alternate encoding may sit beside the universal file, never in place of it. No plan states a measured Safari result for VP9 or AV1.
nodes.norm_label: h.264 and aac in mp4 for every published video

nodes.label: probeBundledVideo() HEAD probe
nodes.rationale: A HEAD request to BUNDLED_VIDEO_SRC so the app can tell a missing clip from a broken one. It caches only a definite answer for the life of the page: 2xx means present, 404 or 410 means absent, and any other status or a failed fetch reports absent for that call alone so the next call retries.

nodes.label: Clip excluded from precache, served CacheFirst
nodes.rationale: Precaching would make every install download the whole clip before the app could work offline, so vite.config.ts excludes it twice: globPatterns never lists mp4, and globIgnores states the exclusion outright so a later edit to globPatterns cannot readmit it. src/sw.ts instead registers a CacheFirst route for same-origin /media/ paths, caching the clip the first time it plays.
nodes.norm_label: clip excluded from precache, served cachefirst

nodes.label: Motivation clip size thresholds
nodes.rationale: 25 MiB warns, 50 MiB triggers a git large-file warning, 100 MiB blocks the push and fails scripts/check-media-size.sh. The 25 MiB guidance is about bandwidth rather than disk: a Pages site carries a soft 100 GB/month limit and every install that triggers the popup downloads the clip once. The separate 150 MiB MAX_VIDEO_BYTES bounds a user-picked clip held in IndexedDB, which never reaches this directory.

nodes.label: User-supplied clip in IndexedDB
nodes.rationale: saveCustomVideo rejects a non-video/ type or a file over MAX_VIDEO_BYTES and writes the clip to IndexedDB (database fti-assets, store videos), never uploading it. IndexedDB is scoped to the browser rather than the profile and saveCustomVideo deletes every other record, so one clip is kept per browser and a second profile replaces the first profile's clip. resolveVideoSrc prefers the stored clip and falls back to the bundled file when the id no longer resolves; the JSON export carries only the asset id.

nodes.label: Inline muted autoplay with tap to unmute
nodes.rationale: WebKit's iOS policy requires playsinline or Safari takes the video fullscreen the moment it plays, and starting playback with sound requires a user gesture. MotivationModal.tsx therefore renders playsinline, autoplay, loop and muted with no transport controls, and a tap unmutes. This supersedes the P6 plan's Play button; master plan section 10.9 records the decision and the reason.
nodes.norm_label: inline muted autoplay with tap to unmute

nodes.label: Optional skin sound effects
nodes.rationale: No audio ships in the repository and none is planned; public/sfx/ holds only .gitkeep. Files go at public/sfx/<skin>/<name>.m4a, the path sfxUrl() builds, and nothing scans the directory. A missing file plays nothing and the app is correct without it. Skins are independent, enforced by the player rather than trusted, and held by the test 'stays silent after a skin change until the next unlock'.

nodes.label: The four fixed sound names
nodes.rationale: session_done on a completed session, pr_stamp when the week stamp lands (timed to the 700 ms landing), rest_over when the rest countdown reaches 0 (the only functional sound, audible in a gym and not like a notification), and intervention_open when the missed-week modal opens (soft and low, never a sting, because it plays over a line about a missed week). There is no fifth.

nodes.label: AAC in .m4a, or MP3, for every published audio asset
nodes.rationale: Master plan section 10.10. Safari plays neither Ogg Vorbis nor WebM, so an Ogg-only or WebM-only asset is silent on every iPhone, the device this app is most likely installed on. A smaller alternate encoding may sit beside the universal file, never in place of it. Every Kenney audio pack ships Ogg Vorbis only, so transcoding is mandatory rather than optional.
nodes.norm_label: aac in .m4a, or mp3, for every published audio asset

nodes.label: Sounds-off-by-default toggle
nodes.rationale: The Settings skin row is the only thing that silences a skin. prefers-reduced-motion is deliberately not consulted: it governs motion, and a user who suppresses animation has said nothing about audio. While the toggle is off the app fetches nothing, so an install that never enables sounds costs the user no bytes even with a directory full of clips.

nodes.label: Gesture unlock and eager decode
nodes.rationale: Browsers refuse to start audio before an interaction, so the app unlocks at three points that each sit inside a real gesture: useFirstGestureUnlock() on the first pointerdown or keydown, the sounds checkbox's own change handler, and the skin picker. Unlocking also decodes all four files for the active skin, because decoding at fire time would add a variable delay and a stamp sound arriving 300 ms late is worse than no sound. A sound is one-shot, never loops, stops the one before it, and stays silent while the tab is backgrounded.

nodes.label: check-sfx-size.sh limits and blind spots
nodes.rationale: Enforces 60 KiB (61440 bytes) per file and 240 KiB (245760 bytes) per skin set, counting only .m4a and .mp3 for the set because one install downloads one file per moment; a 2 s mono clip at 96 kb/s AAC is roughly 24 kB, so 60 KiB is about twice the needed headroom. It fails on an over-limit file, an over-limit set (naming the skin), or an extension with no .m4a or .mp3 sibling. It checks no duration, loudness, channel count, sample rate or decodability, so a corrupt 24 kB file passes CI and is silent. Length and loudness are guidance, not measurements, and no number in the document has been verified.

nodes.label: check-no-emoji.mjs sees tracked files only
nodes.rationale: The emoji gate lists its files with git ls-files, so a component or copy table not yet added to the index is invisible to it and a local run passes on a file CI will scan the moment it is committed. check-sfx-size.sh does not share this blind spot: it walks the tree with find and sees untracked audio as readily as tracked audio.

nodes.label: Sonniss GDC bundles excluded on licence grounds
nodes.rationale: Often described as free to use, they are not CC0. The #GameAudioGDC Bundle Unlimited User License 2.0 is a proprietary royalty-free agreement whose redistribution clause forbids supplying the sound effects as sound effects to any other person without written permission, which is exactly what shipping them in an sfx/ directory would do. Fetched 2026-09-02 and recorded in REFERENCES.md.
nodes.norm_label: sonniss gdc bundles excluded on licence grounds

nodes.label: CC0 audio sources to audition
nodes.rationale: Kenney Interface/Digital/UI Audio, the Freesound CC0 facet and the OpenGameArt CC0 search, carried over from round-three design plan section 6.4. They are candidates to audition rather than selections: the licence is to be verified per file at download time and recorded in REFERENCES.md.

nodes.label: Manual visual check on a phone
nodes.rationale: No pixel in the repository has been measured on a device: every layout claim comes either from jsdom, which renders no geometry, or from a design document stating intent rather than result. Ten rows on two platforms give twenty verdicts, and none can be delegated to an agent because the evidence asked for is a screen. The pass runs installed to the Home Screen, because a tab has different safe-area insets and viewport units, and under the limelight default skin.
nodes.norm_label: manual visual check on a phone

nodes.label: Pink-on-lime contrast failure
nodes.rationale: The limelight pink and lime pair measures 1.41:1 and fails at every size, so pink is a fill, an outline or a shadow and never type on lime. The round-three design plan records the measurement; the phone pass looks for a violation of the rule on a real screen.

nodes.label: Boot line meant to overrun a 320 px phone
nodes.rationale: Each boot step line is 36 characters and is intended to overrun a 320 px phone into a horizontal scroll rather than wrap. A wrapped line is the failure. src/content/copy.ts states that the width is an intent rather than a measured result, in the same file that sets it.
nodes.norm_label: boot line meant to overrun a 320 px phone

nodes.label: SETTINGS_ROWS puts the data row last
nodes.rationale: The wipe control must sit last in Settings and nothing may be appended after the data row, so a destructive action is never reachable before the rows a user actually came for.
nodes.norm_label: settings_rows puts the data row last

nodes.label: Reminder panel state coverage on a phone
nodes.rationale: Seven states exist and eight strings cover them. A build with no Worker origin reaches not-configured and stops, so the panel must be checked on a deployment carrying VITE_REMINDER_API; the state worth the trip is needs-reenable, which an imported document reaches with reminders on and no device.
nodes.norm_label: reminder panel state coverage on a phone

nodes.label: Reaching the migration wizard on a phone
nodes.rationale: Four conditions must hold at once: an fti.console.v2 document in this browser's localStorage, a profile, a plan, and ui.legacyMigration reading pending. Settings can reset that field to pending after a run, which is how the phases explain, preview and applied are re-reached for a visual pass.
nodes.norm_label: reaching the migration wizard on a phone

nodes.label: FTI Console PWA Security Review (2026-09-01)
nodes.rationale: Static read of the fifteen in-scope legacy console files plus five Node reproductions across four timezones, against the GitHub Pages deployment target. Repository had zero commits at review time, so publication findings describe what deploying the tree would create. Counts: 1 Critical, 4 High, 8 Medium, 6 Low, 4 Info.

nodes.label: C1: Unvalidated Import Bricks the App Permanently
nodes.rationale: console-views.jsx:597-620 validates only `typeof parsed !== "object"`, spreads the untrusted object over defaultState(), writes it to localStorage and reloads, so a hostile or stale export becomes boot state. `{"week":999}` makes console-store.jsx:293 dereference PLAN.volume[998] and throw inside the usePlanStore derived useMemo — above every ErrorBoundary — so the tree never mounts and the crash is persisted. Fix: one schema validator gating both rehydration and import, clamped selectors, and an error boundary above the store.
nodes.norm_label: c1: unvalidated import bricks the app permanently

nodes.label: H1: Prescription Medication and Health Profile Shipped as Public Static Assets
nodes.rationale: data.js and console-content.js hard-code body composition (95.3 kg, 27% BF), Vyvanse 40 mg with administration time and pharmacokinetic peak, the supplement stack, and a routine gym location/time; DEPLOY.md:16 instructs uploading data.js. Lisdexamfetamine is a controlled substance, the data is GDPR Art. 9 special-category and directly attributable via the surname in the deployment URL. Git history makes later deletion ineffective.
nodes.norm_label: h1: prescription medication and health profile shipped as public static assets

nodes.label: H2: One-Click Unconfirmed Permanent Data Wipe
nodes.rationale: The `$ rm -rf logs/` footer button (console-app.jsx:179-181) removes fti.console.v2 and reloads with no confirm(), undo or export, on every view — while the sibling reset() does gate on confirm(). With no frame-ancestors and no X-Frame-Options from Pages, one clickjacked tap destroys 24 weeks of logs. The wipe is also partial: fti.plan.v1 and fti.video.instance survive.
nodes.norm_label: h2: one-click unconfirmed permanent data wipe

nodes.label: H3: Silent localStorage Quota Failure Causes Silent Permanent Data Loss
nodes.rationale: saveV2 swallows every storage exception in an empty catch (console-store.jsx:49-51, core.jsx:16, console-video.jsx:64). Past the ~5 MB origin quota — shared with every other project on the account, see M4 — setItem throws QuotaExceededError, the UI still reports success, and everything logged since the first failure is lost on reload with no error ever shown.
nodes.norm_label: h3: silent localstorage quota failure causes silent permanent data loss

nodes.label: H4: Date Helpers Mix UTC and Local Time
nodes.rationale: todayISO and isoOffset round civil dates through toISOString() (UTC) while `new Date(iso+"T00:00:00")` parses as local, and isoDaysBetween subtracts local instants that are not a whole number of days across DST.
