Measured: in Europe/Athens todayISO returns the previous day after 21:00 UTC and isoDaysBetween(2026-01-05, 2026-06-22) = 167 instead of 168; programPosition therefore desynchronises the training day permanently after a DST crossing.
nodes.norm_label: h4: date helpers mix utc and local time

nodes.label: M1: No Content-Security-Policy, and the Architecture Forbids a Strict One
nodes.rationale: GitHub Pages cannot set headers, so a meta tag is the only mechanism, but index.html carries an inline script ('unsafe-inline') and compiles every module in-browser through @babel/standalone ('unsafe-eval'), which voids script-injection protection. The defect is structural; the absent frame-ancestors is what leaves H2's clickjacking path open. Fix: build-time JSX compilation plus a strict meta policy with frame-ancestors 'none'.
nodes.norm_label: m1: no content-security-policy, and the architecture forbids a strict one

nodes.label: M2: Third-Party Video Iframe With No Sandbox on Hardcoded Community Hosts
nodes.rationale: embedUrl is not injectable (11-char YT_ID_RE gate, compile-time host array, encodeURIComponent on search) and referrerPolicy="no-referrer" is correct, but the iframe has no sandbox, so a framed document keeps top-navigation capability under sticky user activation and the four granted permissions. Trust base is six community Invidious hosts fixed at compile time; a lapsed domain re-registered by anyone serves arbitrary JS inside the app.
nodes.norm_label: m2: third-party video iframe with no sandbox on hardcoded community hosts

nodes.label: M3: Service Worker Caches Cross-Origin Scripts Unverified and Fakes Offline Readiness
nodes.rationale: c.add(u).catch(()=>null) discards precache failures so skipWaiting activates an incomplete cache and the app advertises offline support it lacks; unpkg responses are cached with no integrity check, and because the document's SRI still runs, a poisoned entry becomes a permanent hard failure that only a CACHE_NAME bump clears. The `piped.` exclusion is stale (one grep hit, the guard itself). Fix: Workbox via vite-plugin-pwa, bundled deps, origin-based routing.
nodes.norm_label: m3: service worker caches cross-origin scripts unverified and fakes offline readiness

nodes.label: M4: Shared vkotzamanis.github.io Origin Exposes localStorage to Every Other Project
nodes.rationale: Every GitHub Pages project site on one account shares a single origin — the repository name is only a path prefix, and same-origin policy is defined on origin. Any second project, or a dependency it loads, can read fti.console.v2. The quota budget is shared too, which feeds H3. IndexedDB does not help: it is origin-scoped as well.
nodes.norm_label: m4: shared vkotzamanis.github.io origin exposes localstorage to every other project

nodes.label: M5: No Schema Version or Migration; Three Uncoordinated Storage Keys
nodes.rationale: The `v2` in the key name is documentation, not a mechanism: nothing reads a version, there is no migration step, and spreading defaults under persisted data cannot correct a key whose type changed — which is what C1 exploits. Import, export and the wipe button each touch only fti.console.v2, leaving fti.plan.v1 and fti.video.instance stale, so the export is not a complete backup.
nodes.norm_label: m5: no schema version or migration; three uncoordinated storage keys

nodes.label: M6: Primary Set-Log Path Accepts Negative, Unbounded, and Infinite Weight/Reps
nodes.rationale: console-train.jsx:92-99 gates only on !isNaN with no min/max on the inputs, unlike the bounded body-weight and push-up paths. Negative values reach makeCoachLine and suggestedLoad; Infinity arrives through import (JSON.parse('{"weight":1e999}')) and makes core.jsx:92 emit an SVG path of "M 36.0 Infinity", so the chart silently stops drawing. Fix: schema bounds and Number.isFinite, never !isNaN.
nodes.norm_label: m6: primary set-log path accepts negative, unbounded, and infinite weight/reps

nodes.label: M7: waterTarget Drives an Unbounded Render Loop
nodes.rationale: console-views.jsx:199 builds Array.from({length: s.waterTarget}) on the default view. waterTarget has no setter but is persisted, so an imported {"waterTarget": 100000000} freezes and kills the renderer on every load. An ErrorBoundary catches throws, not hangs. Fix: bound it in the schema and clamp every state-derived loop bound at the render site.
nodes.norm_label: m7: watertarget drives an unbounded render loop

nodes.label: M8: Unauthenticated Message Listeners, Wildcard postMessage, and Dev Tooling in Production
nodes.rationale: Neither message listener in tweaks-panel.jsx checks e.origin or e.source, and senders use '*' unconditionally; useTweaks runs from App(), so a framing page receives every tweak change (compounding M1's missing frame-ancestors). 568 lines of a design-tool protocol ship in production, alongside a dead parallel s.tweaks branch in the store that still consumes quota.
nodes.norm_label: m8: unauthenticated message listeners, wildcard postmessage, and dev tooling in production

nodes.label: L1: Google Fonts Stylesheet — No SRI, Client IP Disclosure, Offline Breakage
nodes.rationale: The per-user-agent stylesheet has no stable hash, so SRI is impossible; every load discloses IP and User-Agent to Google in an app whose stated premise is "all data on this device", it is render-blocking, absent from the service worker SHELL, and forces a third party into style-src/font-src. Fix: self-host via @fontsource.
nodes.norm_label: l1: google fonts stylesheet — no sri, client ip disclosure, offline breakage

nodes.label: L2: React Development Builds Served in Production
nodes.rationale: index.html:1496-1497 loads react.development.js and react-dom.development.js — larger, invariant-checking, verbose. SRI hashes are correct and versions pinned, so this is the wrong artifact rather than an unverified one.
nodes.norm_label: l2: react development builds served in production

nodes.label: L3: No Referrer-Policy
nodes.rationale: No <meta name="referrer"> and no header from Pages leaves the browser default (strict-origin-when-cross-origin) unstated and unenforced; the video iframe and links set no-referrer individually.

nodes.label: L4: Service Worker SKIP_WAITING Handler Validates Nothing
nodes.rationale: sw.js:40-44 calls skipWaiting() on any SKIP_WAITING message without checking event.source. Clients are same-origin by definition and the effect is limited to activating an installed worker, so exposure is small.
nodes.norm_label: l4: service worker skip_waiting handler validates nothing

nodes.label: L5: DEPLOY.md Is Inverted Against the Current Tree
nodes.rationale: DEPLOY.md tells the user to upload the stale console.html as index.html and to exclude the real index.html; the two differ by the 20 lines of Invidious instance-rotation CSS the current video modal needs. It also instructs uploading data.js, which is the H1 disclosure path.
nodes.norm_label: l5: deploy.md is inverted against the current tree

nodes.label: L6: Invalid Set Submission Fails Silently
nodes.rationale: submit() returns without effect when parsing fails, and the range-gated body-weight and push-up inputs discard out-of-band values the same way: no message, no focus change, no styling. The user cannot distinguish rejection from success.
nodes.norm_label: l6: invalid set submission fails silently

nodes.label: I1: No XSS Sink Exists Anywhere in the Codebase (Verified Absent)
nodes.rationale: Greps for dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, eval(, new Function, srcdoc and javascript: return zero hits in application code. Every user string reaches the DOM through JSX children, which React escapes.
nodes.norm_label: i1: no xss sink exists anywhere in the codebase (verified absent)

nodes.label: I2: The Import Merge Is Not Prototype-Pollutable (Verified Absent)
nodes.rationale: Object spread copies own enumerable properties by CreateDataProperty, so {"__proto__":{...}} lands as an inert own property. This is a property of the spread operator, not a deliberate guard — Object.assign in the same position would reach the __proto__ setter, so the rewrite must not substitute one for the other.
nodes.norm_label: i2: the import merge is not prototype-pollutable (verified absent)

nodes.label: I3: No Tracking, Analytics, or Outbound Telemetry (Verified Absent)
nodes.rationale: No analytics, beacons, error reporting or WebSocket; the only fetch is sw.js:62 and the "telemetry" in console-store.jsx:178 is a local toast generator.
nodes.norm_label: i3: no tracking, analytics, or outbound telemetry (verified absent)

nodes.label: I4: No Secrets, Keys, or Credentials (Verified Absent)
nodes.rationale: A scan for API keys, tokens, passwords, bearer credentials, AWS/GitHub key prefixes and PEM blocks across all JS/JSX/HTML/JSON returned nothing; the sensitive data was personal (H1), not credential. Superseded on 2026-09-02 by the reminders push credential.
nodes.norm_label: i4: no secrets, keys, or credentials (verified absent)

nodes.label: Absent: URL Injection in the Video Modal
nodes.rationale: videoId is gated by an 11-character [A-Za-z0-9_-] regex, hosts come from a compile-time array, and search terms pass through encodeURIComponent. The missing sandbox (M2) is a privilege problem, not an injection one.
nodes.norm_label: absent: url injection in the video modal

nodes.label: Absent: Insecure Transport
nodes.rationale: No http:// URLs anywhere; GitHub Pages serves HTTPS with HSTS.

nodes.label: Enforceable Constraints for the Rewrite (30 rules)
nodes.rationale: Each of the 30 rules is tied to a finding and phrased so a linter, type checker, test or CI step can fail the build on violation — schema-gated state, bounded numerics, error boundary above the store, one storage key, civil-date arithmetic, strict CSP, bundled dependencies, Workbox precaching, no health data in the tree, and DEV-gated tooling.
nodes.norm_label: enforceable constraints for the rewrite (30 rules)

nodes.label: Review Scope Limits: What Was Not Checked
nodes.rationale: No browser execution, so the C1 black screen, M7 hang and H3 banner absence are inferred from confirmed logic rather than observed. No live HTTP: the three SRI hashes were not recomputed and only DNS resolution of the six Invidious hosts was run. The M3 navigation-redirect breakage is explicitly unverified. design-canvas.jsx, the prototypes, screenshots/ and uploads/ were out of scope, and several files were read only at the named sink classes. Dependency advisories, accessibility and the shared-device threat model were not assessed.
nodes.norm_label: review scope limits: what was not checked

nodes.label: Addendum 2026-09-02: I4 Superseded by the Reminders Push Credential
nodes.rationale: I4 described a console with no server. The P5 reminders work gave the app one, so the document now stores a bearer credential and not only data. Scope is one device's Worker record; the secret is excluded from exports as of that commit but remains unencrypted in localStorage, which is the shared-device threat the review had already declined to raise.
nodes.norm_label: addendum 2026-09-02: i4 superseded by the reminders push credential

nodes.label: AppState.pushDevice.secret (256-bit bearer credential)
nodes.rationale: 43-character base64url CSPRNG value that authorises PUT and DELETE /v1/devices/{id} on the Cloudflare Worker. It reads no data and reaches no other device, but whoever holds it can overwrite or delete that device's reminder schedule. Persisted in the local document under fti.v3.

nodes.label: pushDevice Excluded from Exported Documents
nodes.rationale: exportJson writes "pushDevice": null so a document the user mails, syncs or hands to a helper cannot be used against their Worker record; the live store and the browser's own localStorage copy keep the device, only the file projection drops it. Residual: an imported document with reminderSettings.enabled = true and no device — closed 2026-09-02 in 02dee88 with an explicit "Reminders need enabling again on this device" message.

nodes.label: Single Runtime Schema Gate for Rehydration and Import (Zod/Valibot)
nodes.rationale: One schema is the only entry point into persisted state — localStorage rehydration, file import and paste-import all pass through safeParse, with no `as` cast and no spread of unvalidated data. Reject rather than coerce: keep the last known-good state, show the error, offer export. Bound every numeric field (0 < w <= 500, 1 <= reps <= 100, week 1-24, day 1-7, waterTarget 1-24).
nodes.norm_label: single runtime schema gate for rehydration and import (zod/valibot)

nodes.label: Error Boundary Above the Store Provider
nodes.rationale: The C1 throw happens in the derived useMemo that App() calls before any boundary, so the boundaries around view children never see it. Mounting one above the store keeps a recovery UI that can export and clear state renderable after a store-level throw. Paired with clamped selectors and noUncheckedIndexedAccess so an unvalidated plan-array index is a compile error.
nodes.norm_label: error boundary above the store provider

nodes.label: Explicit schemaVersion and an Ordered Migration Chain
nodes.rationale: An integer schemaVersion inside the payload, ordered pure migrations each tested against a captured fixture of the previous shape, refusal to load a newer version, one storage key, and a round-trip property test parse(serialize(state)) == state that catches the Infinity to null asymmetry.
nodes.norm_label: explicit schemaversion and an ordered migration chain

nodes.label: Civil-Date Arithmetic: date-fns or Temporal, Never toISOString
nodes.rationale: Civil dates must never round-trip through toISOString. Use differenceInCalendarDays/startOfDay or Temporal.PlainDate, whose until() is DST-free by construction, format from getFullYear/getMonth/getDate, persist the user's IANA timezone at setup, and fixture-test Europe/Athens, America/New_York and UTC across both DST transitions with the assertion that a 168-day program measures 168 days everywhere.
nodes.norm_label: civil-date arithmetic: date-fns or temporal, never toisostring

nodes.label: IndexedDB via idb with Surfaced Write Failures
nodes.rationale: Quota is orders of magnitude larger, writes are transactional and genuinely asynchronous, and failures are reportable. QuotaExceededError must raise a blocking banner and offer immediate export; no empty catch around storage, enforced by ESLint no-empty without allowEmptyCatch, plus a test that fills the quota and asserts a visible degraded state.
nodes.norm_label: indexeddb via idb with surfaced write failures

nodes.label: Strict CSP as a Meta Tag (Pages Cannot Set Headers)
nodes.rationale: default-src 'self' with script-src 'self', frame-src pinned to the enumerated Invidious hosts, frame-ancestors 'none', base-uri/form-action/object-src 'none'. Viable only once JSX is compiled at build time and the inline registration script moves into a module, removing 'unsafe-eval' and 'unsafe-inline'. frame-ancestors is honoured in a meta tag by current browsers; report-uri is not.
nodes.norm_label: strict csp as a meta tag (pages cannot set headers)

nodes.label: Clickjacking: No X-Frame-Options and No frame-ancestors
nodes.rationale: GitHub Pages sends no X-Frame-Options and there is no CSP, so any site can frame the app. Combined with a one-click destructive control at a known position (H2), a single overlay click destroys the user's data with no confirmation step to interrupt it.
nodes.norm_label: clickjacking: no x-frame-options and no frame-ancestors

nodes.label: Third-Party Iframe Sandbox Without allow-top-navigation
nodes.rationale: sandbox="allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-presentation", keeping referrerPolicy="no-referrer" and pinning the hosts in frame-src so the browser enforces the allowlist independently of the array. Prefer one well-governed instance over rotating through six.

nodes.label: Hardcoded Invidious Community Instance List
nodes.rationale: Six community-run hosts fixed at compile time, including hobbyist domains; all six resolved in DNS on 2026-09-01, so none is currently abandoned. The structural risk is re-registration of a lapsed domain, after which the app keeps trying it because the list cannot change without a redeploy — hence moving it to runtime configuration.

nodes.label: Service Worker via vite-plugin-pwa and Workbox
nodes.rationale: Content-hashed, all-or-nothing precaching so a failed precache fails the install visibly instead of advertising offline support that does not exist; StaleWhileRevalidate with explicit expiration for same-origin assets and NetworkOnly for third parties, matched by origin rather than String.includes, which matches substrings anywhere in the URL.
nodes.norm_label: service worker via vite-plugin-pwa and workbox

nodes.label: Unverified Cross-Origin unpkg Caching Against Document SRI
nodes.rationale: cache.add and cache.put do not consult the SRI hashes that live on the script tags, so the service worker can store a response the document will then reject. The failure mode is not execution of poisoned code but a permanent unrecoverable boot failure, because cached || network prefers the bad copy and only a CACHE_NAME bump clears it.
nodes.norm_label: unverified cross-origin unpkg caching against document sri

nodes.label: In-Browser JSX Compilation Forces unsafe-eval
nodes.rationale: @babel/standalone compiles every type="text/babel" module in the browser and evaluates it, so any CSP must permit 'unsafe-eval' alongside the inline script's 'unsafe-inline'. That combination provides essentially no script-injection protection, which is why the CSP defect is structural rather than a missing tag.

nodes.label: Number.isFinite, Never !isNaN
nodes.rationale: isNaN(Infinity) is false, which is precisely the gap in the set-log path: Infinity survives the guard, reaches chart scaling as a literal "Infinity" in an SVG d attribute, and JSON.stringify writes it back out as null on export.

nodes.label: CI Grep Gate on Medication and Biometric Identifiers
nodes.rationale: git grep -nEi 'vyvanse|lisdexamfetamine|bf_pct|weight_kg' over tracked source must return nothing, so the H1 disclosure cannot be reintroduced silently. PLAN ships as a neutral template and subject data lives in validated user state entered at setup; any committed occurrence requires history rewrite, not a follow-up commit.
nodes.norm_label: ci grep gate on medication and biometric identifiers

nodes.label: GDPR Article 9 Special-Category Health Data
nodes.rationale: Body composition, a named controlled substance with dose and timing, and a daily routine with location constitute special-category health data, and the deployment URL carries the subject's surname, so the data is directly attributable rather than pseudonymous.

nodes.label: Vyvanse / Lisdexamfetamine 40 mg (Controlled Substance)
nodes.rationale: Named drug, exact dose and administration time appear in data.js, the meal table, the specimen-card content and a VyvanseCurve UI component, plus a COMPOUND_LIFTS RPE gate commented as the Vyvanse-plus-caffeine rule. Disclosure to an employer, insurer or immigration authority is permanent and non-retractable.

nodes.label: GitHub Pages Project Sites Share One Origin
nodes.rationale: The repository name is only a path prefix and same-origin policy is defined on origin, so every project site on one account shares web storage and its quota. Hosting health data in web storage is therefore a hosting decision — a custom domain or dedicated user site — not a code change.
nodes.norm_label: github pages project sites share one origin

nodes.label: Self-Hosted Fonts via @fontsource
nodes.rationale: Google's per-user-agent stylesheet has no stable hash so SRI cannot apply; bundling the families through @fontsource lets style-src 'self'; font-src 'self' hold, keeps fonts working offline in the installed PWA, and discloses nothing to a third party.
